Author(s): Shilong Jing, Yisa Zhang, Yuchen Zhao, Guangsha Guo, Xianda Xu, Hechong Wang, Hengyi Lv, Yang Feng

title: Physically Motivated Knowledge Distillation for Blind Geometric Correction of Side-Scan Sonar Imagery
content: Side-scan sonar (SSS) imagery is susceptible to geometric distortions caused by platform motion instability, which degrade geometric consistency and limit downstream analyses such as mosaicking and perception. Conventional correction methods typically rely on navigation and attitude measurements, which are often unreliable in real ocean conditions. This unreliability necessitates blind geometric correction from a single distorted image a highly ill-posed problem. To address this issue, we propose a physically motivated knowledge distillation framework for blind geometric correction of SSS imagery. Specifically, a teacher network is trained using paired distorted and geocoded reference images to learn distortion-related geometric differences, and this knowledge is transferred to a student network that performs correction using only a single distorted image during blind inference. To ensure physically plausible deformation estimation, we design a parametric decoder that represents distortions as row-wise affine transformations consistent with the SSS line-scanning imaging mechanism. To compensate for the absence of reference information during blind inference, a hallucination context module (HCM) is introduced to approximate the teacher’s geometric reasoning from distorted features under a multilevel distillation scheme. In addition, a differentiable forward warping strategy is adopted to handle the nonbijective deformation characteristics of SSS imagery in an end-to-end manner. Extensive experiments on multiple datasets show that the proposed method outperforms state-of-the-art baselines and generalizes well across different platforms and acquisition conditions.
author: Can Lei, Hayat Rajani, Valerio Franchi, Rafael Garcia, Nuno Gracias, Huigang Wang, Wei Qiang

title: Structure-Aware Multiprototype Prompting Method for Remote Sensing Farmland Segmentation
content: The segment anything model (SAM) has demonstrated remarkable potential for general-purpose visual segmentation. However, adapting SAM for remote sensing farmland image segmentation typically requires extensive pixel-level annotations and carefully designed point- or bounding-box prompts. Moreover, SAM has a limited capability to capture high-frequency structural details, which makes it difficult to precisely localize the complex and irregular boundaries of farmland parcels. To address these issues, we propose a structure-aware multiprototype prompt learning (SMPPL) method for accurate farmland segmentation. First, a structure-aware encoder is designed to progressively enhance farmland structural features with the hierarchical semantic features extracted from the SAM model. Then, a semantic–structure coordination module (SSCM) is developed to align semantic and structural representations through a dual-branch state-space architecture, thereby enabling structure-guided semantic refinement. By integrating these disparate feature spaces, the SSCM is able to reinforce the spatial dependency modeling of farmland parcels. Finally, a multiprototype-guided prompt module (MPGPM) is designed to capture high intraclass variance and automate prompt generation. This mechanism can effectively eliminate the need for manual prompt engineering and enhance the model’s perception of parcel boundaries and regional integrity. On the FarmSeg-VL dataset, SMPPL achieves an intersection over union (IoU) of 86.22% and a Dice score of 91.45%, outperforming current state-of-the-art (SOTA) methods. The method also maintains consistent performance on other public remote sensing datasets, demonstrating its superior segmentation accuracy and robust generalization ability.
author: Miaoxin Lai, Yapeng Gao, Hongxia Deng, Hong Gao, Haifang Li

title: GCCANet: A Small-Object Sensitive and Environment-Robust Network for Remote Sensing Change Detection
content: Remote sensing change detection (RSCD), widely used in industrial and military applications, aims to accurately identify surface changes by comparing two temporally separated images of the same region. In recent years, deep learning has greatly advanced the development of RSCD. However, in complex environments, subtle and background-induced changes often compromise the accuracy of change detection (CD). To address these challenges, we propose the global-context and change-aware network (GCCANet). We adopt a dual-encoder architecture to extract rich semantic features and design an adaptive layer attention (ALA) module that condenses multilevel Transformer semantics into compact global guidance. We further design a background suppression module (BSM) to inject this global guidance into each convolutional neural network (CNN) stage, effectively suppressing background noise and stabilizing the subsequent differencing process. Moreover, we design a difference learning module (DLM) that couples local differencing with global attention matching to extract robust and detail-aware change cues. Then, we introduce a lightweight decoder equipped with a multiscale small-object enhancement (MS-SOE) strategy to enhance subtle changes and preserve thin structures. Extensive experiments on five public benchmark datasets demonstrate that GCCANet consistently achieves state-of-the-art (SOTA) performance. The code is available at https://github.com/E1ison/GCCANet
author: Jingqi Chen, Yonghong Song, Yifei Gao, You Su, Yong Yu

title: CORE-Det: Computation Reallocation for Large-Scene SAR Target Detection
content: Large-scene synthetic aperture radar (SAR) target detection suffers from inefficient computation allocation because most processing is spent on background regions rather than target regions. We propose CORE-Det, a computation reallocation framework that dynamically redistributes processing across spatial regions, feature tokens, and training samples through a three-level sparsity-aware design tailored to SAR electromagnetic scattering. At the spatial level, the computation allocation via spatial distribution (COSD) module reconstructs a dynamic global spatial prior from sparse full-scene observations, performs patch-level screening before local detection, and fuses global and local confidence estimates to suppress background-generated target-like clutter. At the feature level, the computation allocation via feature value (COFV) module introduces SAR-aware mixture-of-experts routing, where specialist experts focus on target-dominant responses produced by strong scattering mechanisms, identity experts preserve structured contextual information at low cost, and zero experts suppress speckle-dominant and invalid activations. At the sample level, the decoupled error partitioning for adaptive retraining (DEPART) module mines hard cases caused by SAR scattering ambiguity and feeds module-specific error signals back to COSD and COFV, improving their ability to separate target-bearing regions from clutter and to distinguish target-dominant, contextual, and noise-dominant responses. Experiments on the self-built FUSAR-Airport and FUSAR-Harbor datasets with six baseline detectors show that CORE-Det consistently improves the accuracy-efficiency tradeoff. Compared with the corresponding baselines, it reduces GFLOPs by 88.92% and inference time by 51.97% on average, while improving mAP50 and recall by 9.59 and 8.94 percentage points (pp), respectively, and reducing false alarms by 19.61 pp.
author: Yuheng Zhang, Muxi Tang, Hecheng Jia, Haipeng Wang

title: Radial Ocean Current Velocity Estimation Errors in TOPSAR Mode: Mechanisms and Correction Method
content: Accurate estimation of radial ocean surface currents (OSCs) from synthetic aperture radar (SAR) Doppler measurements is essential for understanding upper ocean dynamics. However, in the Terrain Observation by Progressive Scans SAR (TOPSAR) mode, as employed by the Sentinel-1 interferometric wide swath (IW) acquisition, the azimuth beam steering introduces a strong coupling between Doppler shifts and azimuthal displacements, resulting in a systematic bias known as the scan-induced Doppler error (SIDE). This study establishes a theoretical signal model describing the motion-induced Doppler characteristics of TOPSAR acquisitions and analytically derives the error mechanism responsible for SIDE. Based on this formulation, an SAR system-based correction model is proposed to compensate for the inherent underestimation of radial velocity (RVL) in the standard Sentinel-1 Level-2 OCN product. Using typical Sentinel-1 operational parameters (antenna azimuth steering rate, ground velocity, and slant range), the analysis reveals that the retrieved radial OSC is underestimated by a factor of 1.08–1.3. This underestimation is identified as a systematic bias intrinsic to the hardware and acquisition geometry of the TOPSAR mode, distinct from geophysical modeling errors. Validation against high-frequency (HF) radar and drifter observations demonstrates that the proposed correction improves retrieval accuracy compared to the conventional CDOP-based approach. Specifically, the method reduces the mean bias from 0.149 to 0.059 m/s and lowers the mean root-mean-square error (RMSE) from 0.260 to 0.222 m/s. These results represent a 60.4% average reduction in mean bias and a 14.6% average reduction in mean RMSE, confirming the effectiveness of the proposed systematic error compensation under both moderate and high sea states, as well as its consistent performance across different subswaths and incidence angles. These findings clarify the origin of Doppler biases in TOPSAR systems and provide a practical framework for improving the accuracy of SAR-derived OSC products in wide-swath imaging modes.
author: Jian Wang, Yuting Zhu, Xiaoqing Wang, Kuan Wang, Shengren Fan, Lixiang Ma

title: Unsupervised Deformable Bilinear Fusion Network for Unregistered Hyperspectral Image Super-Resolution
content: Hyperspectral image super-resolution (HSI-SR) aims to reconstruct a high-resolution hyperspectral image (HrHSI) by fusing a low-resolution hyperspectral image (HSI) with a high-resolution multispectral image (MSI). In practical HSI–MSI fusion, spatial misregistration and nonlinear spectral mixing often occur simultaneously, whereas many existing methods assume accurate registration or rely mainly on linear mixing models (LMMs). To address these issues, we propose an unsupervised deformable bilinear fusion network (UDBFN). The UDBFN integrates a hierarchical registration module (HRM) for multiscale abundance alignment, a cross-modality Transformer (CMT) for estimating cross-modal displacement fields, and a bilinear decoder for modeling linear and pairwise nonlinear mixing components. Experiments on three benchmark datasets show that the UDBFN provides competitive reconstruction accuracy under well-registered settings and is particularly robust under rotation, translation, and nonrigid misregistration. The code is available at https://github.com/zoukeh/UMDBN-master
author: Hao Zhu, Kehanling Zou, Yunkai Zou, Yongxu Liu, Jinjian Wu

title: FG-MoE: Frequency-Guided Mixture of Experts for Unified Remote Sensing Image Restoration
content: In remote sensing (RS), image restoration is an essential but difficult problem because degradation patterns are diverse and scene content is highly heterogeneous. Existing RS image restoration methods still exhibit two major weaknesses: 1) they are built for a single degradation category, resulting in limited generalization across diverse restoration tasks; and 2) they process all frequency components of the image uniformly, making it difficult to reconstruct both global semantics and fine textures. In this article, we propose a frequency-guided mixture-of-experts (FG-MoE) framework, which enables unified RS image restoration across diverse degradation types by leveraging frequency-aware modeling to achieve accurate recovery of both semantic information and fine details. Specifically, FG-MoE consists of three key modules. First, we introduce the frequency mask prediction module (FMPM), which utilizes the fast Fourier transform (FFT) to generate frequency-aware masks for separating low- and high-frequency components. Guided by these masks, we design a frequency-guided mixture-of-experts (FG-MoE) module that dynamically assigns frequency components to specialized expert branches for targeted degradation processing. Furthermore, an expert fusion module (EFM) is proposed to adaptively integrate the outputs of both branches, enabling comprehensive and balanced reconstruction. Comprehensive experiments show that FG-MoE delivers strong restoration results under diverse RS image degradation conditions, including dehazing, cloud removal, and low-light enhancement.
author: Mingwen Shao, Jie Zhang, Shanshan Song, Xiangyong Cao

title: Radiometric Intercalibration of Multisource Nighttime Light Images at High Resolution for Disaster Mapping
content: High-resolution nighttime light (NTL) remote sensing has become increasingly important for detailed and timely disaster assessment. However, the long revisit cycles of high-resolution satellites constrain continuous disaster monitoring, making multisource image integration necessary for enhancing temporal frequency. Radiometric intercalibration is, therefore, required to bridge sensor differences and ensure comparability of NTL images. Previous intercalibration methods rely on the pseudoinvariant pixel (PIP) framework, typically selecting PIPs based on socioeconomic stability assumptions or images acquired on overlapping dates. These methods are inapplicable in disaster scenarios because cross-sensor images are rarely obtained simultaneously and may exhibit substantial NTL changes. In this study, we proposed an automatic radiometric intercalibration framework for high-resolution NTL images, using SDGSAT-1 and Yangwang-1 as a case study. The proposed method automatically identified PIPs from preevent and postevent images with dramatic changes, which were then used to establish a patch-to-pixel transformation from the SDGSAT-1 image to the Yangwang-1 image. The nonlinear relationship of the transformation was learned using random forest (RF), enabling the intercalibration of SDGSAT-1 to Yangwang-1-like images. The method was applied to two disaster events (i.e., the Israel–Gaza war and the Türkiye–Syria earthquake) and was evaluated using reference PIPs as validation data. In these reference pseudoinvariant regions, the accuracy of the method was measured by measuring the consistency between NTL values of Yangwang-1 and Yangwang-1-like (i.e., the intercalibrated SDGSAT-1). The results demonstrated high accuracy of our method, with R2 values of 0.94 and 0.89 for the two events, respectively, which are better than two conventional methods. The proposed framework can be extended to the integration of other multisource NTL images in disaster scenarios, supporting emergency mapping for humanitarian relief.
author: Xi Li, Shuai Jiang

title: 3-D Adaptive GNSS Tomography Fusing Pangu-Weather-Derived Water Vapor Gradient and Signal Density Fields
content: The illposed nature of observation equations, due to the sparsity of global navigation satellite system (GNSS) observation signals, remains a core challenge in water vapor tomography. Traditional static fixed-grid methods have limitations in addressing the sparsity of GNSS signals and the complexities of atmospheric water vapor. To address this problem, we propose a gradient-signal adaptive grid (GSAG) generation method constrained by both signal density and water vapor gradients. The core of GSAG involves constructing a gradient-signal field (GSF) that integrates dual information: first, a continuous signal density field is constructed using radial basis function (RBF) interpolation to assess the feasibility of refinement. Second, the water vapor gradient is calculated using the background field forecast by the Pangu-Weather model to identify the necessity of refinement. Validated against radiosonde data, the average root-mean-square error (RMSE) of GSAG decreased from 1.3970 to 0.9756 g/m3 (30.2%), and the average mean absolute error (MAE) declined from 1.1180 to 0.7696 g/m3 (31.2%) relative to the conventional fixed grid (FG) method. Qualitative analysis shows that GSAG effectively captures detailed mesoscale features, including key water vapor convergence zones that preceded extreme rainfall, whereas the FG method tends to overly smooth essential information. The proposed GSAG method significantly enhances the application potential of GNSS tomography in meteorological nowcasting and early warning.
author: Yuqing Liu, Qi Zhang, Chaoqian Xu, Xiongwei Ma, Youkun Wang, Xiuguang Yao, Yibin Yao, Yunzheng Huang

title: Resilient Unsupervised Deep Learning for Data Denoising via Noise-to-Semiclean Training
content: Seismic data denoising is crucial for improving signal quality in both passive seismic monitoring and active subsurface exploration, enabling more reliable interpretation. In this work, a novel unsupervised deep learning approach with robust learning is proposed for denoising seismic data. The method begins by transforming the seismic data into a 2-D representation. This transformation extracts localized time–frequency features that capture the signal’s frequency variation over time. To enhance the robustness of the deep neural network’s learning process, a self-noise cancellation stage based on vector space projections is incorporated. This allows the network to learn sparse representations of the signals, achieved through a specifically tailored loss function. Comparative evaluations demonstrate that the proposed method achieves a strong denoising performance, with an average signal-to-noise ratio (SNR) improvement of 15 dB, by effectively learning sparse features. Benchmarked against other unsupervised methods, it consistently shows superior performance. Extensive experiments on synthetic, pseudosynthetic, and field datasets further validate its effectiveness in significantly enhancing the SNR of seismic data. The proposed framework is validated on passive seismic data and shows strong potential for extension to active seismic scenarios, as well as to general signal enhancement applications, including audio signal processing, biomedical, wireless communications, and radar systems.
author: Yaser Almasri, Naveed Iqbal, Mudassir Masood

title: An Integrated Image Matching and Block Adjustment Method for Regional-Scale Spaceborne SAR Image Mapping
content: The rapid development of spaceborne synthetic aperture radar (SAR) systems has provided abundant data for Earth observation. However, their initial relative geometric positioning accuracy remains insufficient for regional-scale SAR image mapping. To address this challenge, an integrated method combining image matching and block adjustment is proposed. First, regional-scale SAR image matching is decomposed into parallelizable slice image matching based on grid division of geographic overlapping areas. An enhanced SAR-scale-invariant feature transform (SIFT) (ESAR-SIFT) algorithm is developed to extract reliable tie points (TPs) from slice images while preserving more edge details and mitigating neighboring feature interference. Next, the extracted TPs are mapped to the whole SAR image through a geometric transformation model, and a joint geometric–radiometric constraint-based adaptive nonmaximum suppression algorithm is proposed to achieve a spatially homogenized distribution of TPs. Finally, using these TPs, a digital elevation model-aided planar block adjustment model is established to estimate the orientation parameters of all images and generate orthorectified images. Experiments on 16 LuTan-1 (LT-1) and 4 GaoFen-3 (GF-3) images validate the effectiveness of the proposed method. The ESAR-SIFT algorithm demonstrates superior performance in both matching quantity and accuracy across diverse terrains. The root mean square errors of homogenized TPs are reduced from 4.034 pixels to 0.731 pixels for LT-1 and from 3.567 pixels to 0.702 pixels for GF-3. The resulting relative positioning accuracies reach 0.56 m for LT-1 (3-m resolution) and 8.43 m for GF-3 (10-m resolution). These results confirm that the proposed method enables accurate and efficient regional-scale SAR image mapping.
author: Ming Xia, Tuwang Li, Bo Zhang, Lihua Li, Chao Wang

title: Stage-Adaptive Spatial-Frequency Decomposition and Enhancement With Multimodal Conditional Routing for Remote Sensing Image Segmentation
content: Multimodal remote sensing image segmentation benefits from complementary cues provided by heterogeneous data sources, but accurate segmentation remains challenging due to difficulties in effectively fusing multimodal features and preserving fine-grained structures. Although spatial-frequency fusion methods have shown promise, existing approaches often rely on fixed or input-agnostic frequency partitioning and overlook the different objectives of encoding and decoding stages, limiting their adaptability to scene-dependent frequency distributions and stage-specific representation needs. To address these limitations, we propose a stage-adaptive spatial-frequency decomposition and enhancement network (SF-DENet) for multimodal remote sensing image segmentation. SF-DENet adopts a two-stream encoder–decoder architecture and introduces two stage-specific spatial-frequency fusion modules with distinct interaction patterns. During encoding, the encoder spatial-frequency fusion (EnFusion) module feeds the fused optical–auxiliary features into parallel spatial and frequency branches and employs adaptive frequency masks to modulate the amplitude spectrum, thereby enhancing cross-modal semantic alignment. During decoding, the decoder spatial-frequency fusion (DeFusion) module introduces explicit high- and low-frequency cues guided by the original inputs and performs frequency-aware interaction between decoder features and skip-connected encoder features, thereby enhancing structure-aware detail reconstruction. To overcome fixed or input-agnostic frequency partitioning, the frequency branch incorporates a conditional composition-based frequency decomposition (C$^{2}$FD) module, which predicts routing weights from multimodal inputs and composes multiple soft-edge frequency-mask experts into content-adaptive masks for frequency representation modulation. Experiments on multiple multimodal remote sensing benchmarks demonstrate that SF-DENet achieves superior segmentation performance, particularly in scenes with complex textures, ambiguous boundaries, and modality inconsistency.
author: Xuran Pan, Rui Zhang, Zibo Xu, Tingting Zhao

title: Assessing the DINEOF Algorithm for Spatiotemporal Reconstruction of Multisource Remote Sensing Data in Inland Lakes: A Case Study of Lake Dianchi
content: Satellite remote sensing is critical for lake monitoring but is often hindered by data gaps arising from clouds and sensor malfunctions. To explore the feasibility of current gap filling solutions for inland lakes, this article took Lake Dianchi (2020–2023) in southwestern China as a representative case and comprehensively evaluated the performance of the data interpolating empirical orthogonal functions (DINEOF) algorithm for reconstructing missing remote sensing observations under complex weather conditions. The impacts of missing data proportion, gap size, spectral waveband, and spatial resolutions on the algorithm were assessed using medium-to-low resolution datasets (MODIS and Ocean and Land Color Instrument; 500 m) and medium-to-high resolution datasets (OLI and MSI; 30 m). The results showed that DINEOF remained reliable for medium-to-low resolution data when the missing proportion was below 70% (R2 > 0.65, root mean square error <0.0013 sr−1), beyond which the reconstruction accuracy declined sharply. Performance is more sensitive to the overall missing proportion than to individual gap size, and their combined effects lead to nonlinear degradation. Despite reduced accuracy under high missing conditions, DINEOF outperformed a conventional Kriging–Savitzky–Golay approach, which even yielded negative R2 values. Clear spectral dependence is observed, with better performance in the red and green bands than in the blue band. In contrast, DINEOF performs poorly for medium-to-high resolution data, showing lower accuracy and pronounced patch-like artifacts. Overall, DINEOF is effective for reconstructing medium-to-low resolution lake data within a threshold of missingness, but more advanced methods are needed for higher resolution data in complex aquatic environments.
author: Peixin Chen, Zhenyu Tan, Zhuting Tan, Zhigang Cao

title: CHSG: A Center-Aware Axial Hierarchical Sparse Graph Network for Hyperspectral Image Classification
content: Hyperspectral image (HSI) classification requires capturing both global geometric structures and fine-grained local details. While graph neural networks (GNNs) offer powerful topological modeling, standard explicit graph construction suffers from two critical limitations: prohibitive resource consumption and the introduction of background noise that dilutes the spectral fidelity of the center pixel. Moreover, the smoothing nature of GNNs often leads to the loss of high-frequency local textures. To overcome these challenges, we propose the center-aware axial hierarchical sparse graph network (CHSG), a sparse graph learning framework designed to balance global topological reasoning with local detail preservation while avoiding explicit graph construction. First, the hierarchical sparse graph attention (HSGA) module employs an axial rolling strategy to achieve implicit graph topological awareness. Rather than calculating computationally intensive pairwise affinities, it functions as a directional aggregator that encodes topological continuity through roll-based neighborhood aggregation, effectively capturing anisotropic spatial structures. Second, the center-aware positional encoding (CAPE) module treats the target pixel as a spectral anchor, generating content-adaptive attention to explicitly filter out heterogeneous interference. Finally, a parallel spectral–spatial joint multiscale (SSJM) module serves as a texture compensator by aggregating multiscale spectral–spatial contexts to recover diverse local patterns smoothed out by the graph branch. Experiments on four benchmark datasets demonstrate that CHSG achieves state-of-the-art accuracy while maintaining a favorable balance between classification performance and computational cost.
author: Lianlian Zhao, Lina Yang, Zhiyang You, Guanyu Qin, Xinzhang Wu, Haoyan Yang, Gang Chen

title: Deep-Sea Bathymetry From Geosynchronous SAR via DTCWT-Enhanced Spatial-Correlation Wave Imaging and Multiparameter Time-Series Inversion
content: Deep-sea bathymetry inversion from geosynchronous synthetic aperture radar (GEO SAR) offers persistent wide-area monitoring capabilities but faces two fundamental challenges: the defocusing of topography-induced sea-surface waves due to their nonlinear space-variant motions during long integration times, and the ill-posed nature of retrieving seabed topography from surface signatures due to the nonlinear, depth-dependent filtering effect of the stratified water column. To address these issues, this article builds upon our previous GEO spatial-correlation (SC) SAR spatial-correlation imaging framework and existing sea-surface parameter retrieval modules, and introduces two new components for this task: a GEO dual-tree complex wavelet transform (DTCWT)-SC SAR imaging algorithm and a StratiFormer inversion network. On the imaging side, we develop the GEO DTCWT-SC SAR algorithm: oriented DTCWT subbands represent nonlinear, space-variant kinematics with a set of direction-separable and 2-D cross-directional residual modes that parameterize a motion-compensated spatial-correlation kernel. Applied point-by-point to the echoes, this kernel corrects the phase history, restores the slow-time spatial correlation of the sea-surface pattern, and enables closed-loop, correlation-driven motion refinement. On the inversion side, we introduce StratiFormer, a hierarchical spatiotemporal network that performs multiparameter time-series inversion from sea-surface height and 2-D current sequences to deep-sea bathymetry. Unlike static image-to-depth models, StratiFormer ingests the multiparameter time series into a three-stage hierarchical encoder with learnable interstage feature fusion. The hybrid-phase decoupling and current-retrieval steps are used as an integrated retrieval and observation–construction interface rather than as new contributions of this article. Controlled echo-to-depth simulations, reanalysis-informed surface-field experiments, and terrain-disjoint diagnostics support the algorithmic feasibility of the proposed workflow under controlled and reanalysis-informed settings, while operational validation with measured GEO-SAR observations and collocated bathymetric truth remains necessary.
author: Yuhang Li, Mei Liu, Xuemei Sui

title: FSDNet: Joint Frequency-Spatial Modulation Network for Remote Sensing Image Dehazing
content: Remote sensing image dehazing is a critical preprocessing step for numerous downstream Earth observation tasks, including object detection, postdisaster damage assessment, and urban expansion monitoring. However, this task remains inherently challenging due to haze-induced atmospheric scattering, which severely degrades key visual attributes—particularly global contrast, edge definition, and high-frequency structural details. Such degradation directly impairs the reliability and accuracy of subsequent analytical pipelines. While conventional spatial-domain convolutional neural networks (CNNs) have achieved notable performance, they often suffer from excessive smoothing of fine-scale edges and textures. More recent Transformer- and diffusion-based approaches, though promising, incur prohibitive computational overhead and memory demands—limiting their practical deployment in resource-constrained remote sensing workflows. To bridge this gap, we propose FSDNet, a lightweight joint frequency-spatial modulation network that explicitly decouples and jointly optimizes spatial and frequency representations. Central to our design is the frequency-spatial dual-branch block (FSDBlock): the spatial branch leverages a multiscale pyramidal perception module—integrating depthwise and strip convolutions in parallel—to efficiently capture both global context and local structural cues across heterogeneous receptive fields; the frequency branch (FGB) operates in the Fourier domain, employing an adaptive amplitude mask guided by FFT to selectively attenuate haze-corrupted low-frequency components. Furthermore, we introduce a dedicated frequency reconstruction loss ($L_{\text{FFT}}$) that enforces fidelity between the predicted and GT amplitude spectra, thereby preserving essential frequency-domain structures. Comprehensive evaluations on multiple benchmark remote sensing dehazing datasets consistently demonstrate that FSDNet achieves strong restoration performance while maintaining low computational cost, memory usage, and inference latency.
author: Xiaohui Dong, Yuanming Lu, Haoming Su, Chengchao Wang

title: SAR Image Object Detection Based on Cascaded Denoising and Counterfactual Self-Distillation
content: Background noise in synthetic aperture radar (SAR) images can severely degrade object detection performance. Although many methods employ complex image denoising strategies, target features in SAR imagery are tightly coupled with background noise. Meanwhile, excessive pixel-level smoothing inevitably weakens critical scattering details, resulting in the loss of discriminative and localization-relevant information. To address the above challenges, a cascaded denoising and counterfactual self-distillation framework for SAR object detection (CDC-DETR) is proposed. By jointly optimizing multiple components of the detection model, CDC-DETR builds a multistage denoising architecture that suppresses noise while preserving critical target details. Specifically, a frequency-domain feature fusion module is introduced, which adaptively integrates features from different frequency bands through a gated mechanism. In addition, a background-aware encoder denoising module is designed to compute feature statistics guided by target semantic priors, enabling weighted suppression of interference from different background regions. This design encourages the model to focus on target areas while preserving relevant contextual information. Furthermore, to enhance discriminative target feature extraction, CDC-DETR incorporates a counterfactual self-distillation mechanism that derives counterfactual information from deformable attention maps and guides self-correction during training, thereby preventing the loss of semantic cues in background–target coupled regions. Extensive experiments on MSAR and CETC38-SAR datasets demonstrate the efficiency of the proposed method when compared with state-of-the-art techniques.
author: Luyun Tian, Yinju Nie, Guangjun He, Jie Geng, Wen Jiang, Shichao Jin

title: New Insights Into the Structural Health of Super High-rise Buildings in Severe Convective Weather From Ground-Based Radar Interferometry
content: In recent years, the increasing frequency of global natural disasters and severe convective weather (SCW) events, driven by climate change, has heightened the vulnerability of the coastal areas of the Guangdong–Hong Kong–Macao Greater Bay Area (GBA) in China. These regions, characterized by high population density and densely concentrated infrastructure, are particularly susceptible to SCW-related hazards. Among these infrastructures, super high-rise buildings are especially sensitive to wind-induced vibrations due to their high flexibility and low fundamental frequency, placing them at significant risk of structural damage when subjected to severe wind loads during SCW events. Although traditional sensors and wind tunnel experiments are effective tools for the structural health monitoring (SHM) of super high-rise buildings, they are limited by high costs, low resolution, and restricted measurement coverage. In this article, we for the first time utilize the gamma portable radar interferometer (GPRI) to observe coastal super high-rise buildings and obtain the natural frequencies and vibration modes before, during, and after an SCW event. A novel positioning method of GPRI measurement is proposed to resolve the localization ambiguity issue commonly encountered in GPRI monitoring. The results validate the feasibility of using GPRI for SHM of super high-rise buildings under SCW conditions.
author: Bochen Zhang, Mi Jiang, Deyang Wei, Cheng Feng, Siting Xiong, Hanwen Yu, Xiao Cheng, Zhiwei Li

title: FB-TDF1: A Fuzzy-Boundary, Timeliness- and Dispersion-Weighted Evaluation Metric for Anomaly Detection in Satellite Remote Sensing
content: Machine learning offers substantial potential for improving anomaly detection in satellite telemetry, a task central to spacecraft health monitoring. As modern satellites generate increasingly large volumes of multivariate telemetry, automated detection systems must evolve to reduce the monitoring burden on spacecraft operations engineers (SOEs) and mitigate operational risks. Although numerous time series anomaly detection (TSAD) methods have been proposed, reliably evaluating their performance under realistic telemetry conditions remains a persistent challenge. Recent transformer-based models have demonstrated strong capability in capturing long-range dependencies and multichannel interactions in telemetry and remote sensing data, thereby gaining increasing adoption in TSAD applications. However, these models exhibit characteristic behaviors—such as smooth attention-driven score transitions near event boundaries, sensitivity to weak precursor patterns leading to slight onset misalignment, and multi-head-induced isolated false alarms—that are not adequately handled by existing evaluation metrics. From an operational perspective, an effective metric should reward timely detection, tolerate the inherent ambiguity of expert-annotated anomaly boundaries, penalize dispersed false alarms that substantially increase SOE workload, and discourage the complete omission of anomalous events, since missing an entire spacecraft anomaly may lead to severe operational consequences even if the missed segment is short. To address these limitations, we propose fuzzy-boundary timeliness and dispersion-weighted F-score (FB-TDF1), a new evaluation metric that jointly accounts for i) detection timeliness, ii) boundary uncertainty in expert annotations, iii) the dispersion characteristics of false positives, and iv) event-level missed-anomaly risk through an event-aware recall correction. FB-TDF1 is specifically designed to reflect the behavioral patterns of modern transformer-based TSAD models and align with the practical evaluation needs of real satellite telemetry monitoring systems.
author: Kaixiang Yang, Jiarong Liu, Jian He, Chengrong Yang, Shuanghua Yang, Yujue Zhou

title: STE-RDet: Spatiotemporal-Enhanced Network for Event-Based Rotated Object Detection in Remote Sensing
content: Remote sensing object detection in low-altitude uncrewed aerial vehicle scenarios frequently involves densely distributed targets with arbitrary orientations and large viewpoint changes. Under such conditions, horizontal bounding boxes introduce severe background redundancy, ambiguous overlap, and inaccurate localization, making rotated object detection essential for precise geometry modeling and reliable instance separation. Meanwhile, frame-based sensors suffer from motion blur and limited dynamic range under high-speed maneuvering and drastic illumination variation, which weakens the contour continuity and directional cues required for accurate oriented bounding box regression. Event cameras provide asynchronous microsecond response and high dynamic range, but simply replacing the sensor is insufficient: after voxelization, event streams become sparse spatiotemporal tensors dominated by motion boundaries, while existing remote sensing benchmarks and rotated detectors are largely designed for dense appearance patterns. To address this gap, we construct the rotated event-based remote sensing object detection dataset (RERSOD), the first large-scale benchmark for this task in complex aerial observation conditions. Building on RERSOD, we propose the spatiotemporal-enhanced rotation detection network (STE-RDet), an event-aware rotated detector tailored to voxel-grid representations. STE-RDet explicitly addresses three key bottlenecks in event-based oriented detection: response dilution during upsampling, insufficient coupling between local structure and temporal dynamics, and background-dominated interference during multiscale aggregation. To this end, the framework constrains feature energy redistribution during upsampling, reinforces the interaction between local spatial topology and temporal event dynamics, and calibrates anisotropic context for orientation-sensitive regression. Extensive experiments on RERSOD demonstrate that STE-RDet achieves markedly better accuracy, robustness, and convergence efficiency than strong baselines and state-of-the-art rotated detectors.
author: Zhengwei Qiao, Hailong Liu, Xiangzhi Li, Hengyi Lv, Yang Feng, Yisa Zhang, Shilong Jing, Junyao Sang

title: Multistage Nonlinear Transform Tensor Nuclear Norm for Hyperspectral Image Super-Resolution
content: Hyperspectral image super-resolution (HSI-SR) aims to reconstruct a high-resolution hyperspectral image by fusing a low-resolution hyperspectral image with a high-resolution multispectral image. Tensor nuclear norm (TNN)-based regularization has shown strong potential in model-based HSI-SR by exploiting the intrinsic low-rank structure of hyperspectral data in transform domains. However, existing transform-domain TNN methods are still predominantly formulated in linear representation spaces, including fixed analytical transforms, cascaded linear transforms, and data-adaptive linear transforms. Such linear-domain low-rank priors are insufficient to characterize the nonlinear, nonconvex, and high-order spatial–spectral dependencies widely present in real-world hyperspectral scenes. To address this limitation, this article proposes a multistage nonlinear transform tensor nuclear norm, termed MNTNN, for HSI-SR. The proposed MNTNN imposes tensor low-rankness in a structured nonlinear representation domain rather than in a purely linear transform domain. Specifically, a multistage nonlinear transform is constructed by integrating nonlinear representation mapping, fixed analytical transform anchoring, and data-adaptive subspace alignment, which respectively model high-order nonlinear correlations, global structural regularities, and scene-specific low-rank characteristics. Furthermore, the proposed MNTNN is embedded into a nonlocal patch-based subspace fusion framework, and an efficient alternating direction method of multipliers algorithm is developed to solve the resulting optimization problem. Extensive experiments on simulated and real-world datasets demonstrate that the proposed method achieves competitive or superior reconstruction performance compared with representative state-of-the-art HSI-SR methods, especially in preserving spatial details and spectral fidelity.
author: Zhihui Tu, Yisha Gao, Susu Lv, Wenyu Hu, Jian Lu

title: MEFMA: A Multiscale Empirical Fringe-Manifold Adaptive Filtering Framework for Robust InSAR Phase Restoration
content: In conditions of extremely low signal-to-noise ratio and complex decorrelation, the interferometric synthetic aperture radar (InSAR) phase is often severely corrupted by dense noise. Existing filtering methods struggle to achieve an effective balance among noise suppression, high-frequency topological detail preservation, and the avoidance of nonphysical spurious fringes, thereby constraining the accuracy of subsequent phase unwrapping. To address this issue, this article proposes a multiscale empirical fringe-manifold adaptive filtering (MEFMA) framework. This algorithm constructs a V-cycle-like phase decomposition and cascaded reconstruction framework, which is primarily driven alternately by two nonlinear operators. The first is a spatial-frequency adaptive operator based on Hoyer’s sparsity, enabling the data-driven extraction of local fringe features. The second is a complex gradient constant phase reconstruction smoothing operator, which effectively filters out broadband noise while preserving high-frequency deformation gradients without relying on heavy subspace eigen-decomposition. Furthermore, the algorithm introduces a coherence-based cascaded weighting and terminal gradient smoothing mechanism to suppress the nonlinear propagation and accumulation of errors. Experiments based on complex simulated data and real spaceborne SAR data from the Myanmar earthquake, the Turkey earthquake, and the Etna volcano demonstrate that the MEFMA algorithm outperforms existing comparative methods in metrics such as structural similarity and root mean square error. The proposed algorithm can successfully reconstruct high-frequency dense fringes in low-coherence regions, significantly reduce the number of residue points, and effectively mitigate unwrapped phase jumps caused by topological discontinuities. Consequently, it provides reliable data support for high-precision InSAR inversions in complex geological disaster environments.
author: Jian Li, Hongdong Fan, Huifu Zhuang, Yeerda Yeerdingdala, Sen Du

title: WTUMamba: A Wavelet-Enhanced U-Shaped Mamba Network for Island Segmentation in High-Resolution Remote Sensing Images
content: Accurate island segmentation in high-resolution remote sensing images is essential for ecological conservation. Although deep learning-based methods have achieved significant breakthroughs, the low class separability and the imbalanced class distributions on islands still pose challenges for accurate segmentation. In this article, we propose a wavelet-enhanced U-shaped Mamba network (WTUMamba) for island segmentation. This network comprises two core modules. First, a multilevel frequency-enhanced wavelet convolution module is proposed to enhance the discrimination of features among different ground objects via the multiscale decomposition and reconstruction of wavelet transforms. Second, a spectral-spatial enhanced state space module is designed to enhance feature modeling performance under class-imbalanced conditions while preserving linear computational complexity. Moreover, we construct a new island dataset, namely the Sun Yat-sen University Island Semantic Segmentation dataset, to evaluate the effectiveness of WTUMamba. This dataset comprises 17 islands in the South China Sea region, covering a total area of 12.57 km$^{2}$ and providing manually annotated pixel-wise labels. Additional experiments on the Gaofen Image Dataset are also performed to further evaluate the segmentation performance of WTUMamba. Experimental results demonstrate that WTUMamba achieves superior performance over state-of-the-art methods across core evaluation metrics.
author: Yiming Chen, Zhi He, Chengle Zhou, Jian Dong

title: Symmetry-Enhanced AI and GIS Framework Using Open Data for Simplified Physical Stability Assessment of Tailings Storage Facilities in Chile
content: Globally, the long-term stability of tailings storage facilities is a critical environmental and safety concern, particularly in mining countries such as Chile, which hosts over 836 deposits distributed across highly variable geotechnical and climatic conditions. Traditional assessment frameworks rely heavily on field inspections and site-specific data, limiting their scalability and frequency of evaluation by the national geology and mining service. This study proposes a simplified mechanism for evaluating physical stability based on open-access data processed using artificial intelligence and geographic information systems to obtain an overall condition assessment. This mechanism quantifies two key indicators—the potential impact on the environment and the potential for physical instability—which are integrated into a hierarchical classification to prioritize regulatory supervision. The proposed methodology combines satellite imagery, geographic information layers, and deep learning models for the automatic detection, segmentation, and classification of tailings storage facilities. The systematic injection of rotational symmetries significantly increased the robustness of the segmentation model, evidenced by improvements across multiple evaluation metrics for different facility sizes. In addition, a classification model successfully categorized the distinct topographic configurations of these deposits. The methodology was validated in two major Chilean regions, achieving strong agreement with expert technical evaluations and providing a structured prioritization scheme that enables authorities to improve continuous monitoring and regulatory supervision. Finally, a large language model was implemented to assist in interpreting the simplified evaluation process for nontechnical users, structuring the analytical information into an accessible technical report format.
author: Giovanni Cocca-Guardia, Gabriel Villavicencio, Gabriel Hermosilla, Vinicius Minatogawa, Jorge Rojas-Vivanco, Manuel Silva, Gabriel Olmos, Pierre Breul

title: Human-Cognitive Inspired Remote Sensing Change Detection Network
content: Remote sensing change detection (RSCD) elucidates spatiotemporal land cover dynamics through bitemporal image analysis, thereby providing critical infrastructure for urban expansion monitoring, forest degradation assessment, and disaster response management. Despite advancements in deep learning-based RSCD frameworks, three pivotal limitations persist: first, suboptimal global context modeling, second, insufficient temporal feature encoding, and third, monolithic decision architectures lacking cognitive stratification. To mitigate these challenges, we propose the human cognitive decision-inspired network—a novel RSCD paradigm that reengineers feature representation and information fusion through a biologically plausible four-stage pipeline: perception–memory–observation–decision. In the perception stage, we leverage a pretrained vision foundation model to extract hierarchical multiscale image features, simulating initial human perceptual processing of visual scenes. The memory stage incorporates a bidirectional long short-term memory architecture augmented with channel–spatial attention modules, enabling bidirectional temporal context encoding while selectively reinforcing feature associations in salient change regions. The observation stage introduces a Dense Mamba module that integrates multiscale convolutional kernels with dynamic weight allocation strategies, facilitating efficient global context perception through parallel feature extraction and adaptive fusion. Finally, the decision stage constructs an observation–memory fusion decider that synthesizes multievidence representations through cross-modal attention mechanisms, emulating human collaborative decision-making processes to generate high-fidelity change masks. Notably, we compared our work with 19 state-of-the-art works, including both recent and classical works, showing improved accuracy (via five evaluative metrics) over five benchmark datasets.
author: Wenchao Zhang, Wenhui Ye, Zhenhua Yu, Xiang Li, Yu Zheng

title: SAPLNet: State-Aware Prototype Learning for Remote Sensing Segmentation
content: Semantic segmentation of high-resolution remote sensing images remains challenging due to complex spatial structures, multiscale object variations, fine-grained category differences, and high interclass similarities. Conventional segmentation methods usually rely on fixed convolutional heads or single feature representations, which makes it difficult to effectively model both intraclass appearance variations and interclass texture similarities, often leading to category confusion, missed objects, and incomplete segmentation in complex scenes. To address these challenges, we propose a state-aware prototype learning network, termed SAPLNet. Specifically, a cross-stage state refiner is introduced to progressively refine multilevel features by integrating the input features with the outputs of different stages through state-aware gated normalization. Then, a weighted feature pyramid decoder performs top-down fusion of the refined hierarchical features, combining high-level semantic information with low-level spatial details. Furthermore, a state-aware multiprototype classifier is designed to construct multiple semantic prototypes for each class via ground-truth-guided local class-center extraction and momentum-based prototype memory updating. A global state vector derived from the refined cross-stage features is used to adaptively modulate decoder features, improving the matching reliability between pixel features and class prototypes. In addition, prototype compactness loss, prototype diversity loss, and lightweight boundary loss are employed to enhance intraclass consistency, prototype discriminability, and boundary awareness. Experimental results demonstrate the effectiveness and superiority of SAPLNet.
author: Zeyu Zhao, Zhaolong Gao, Jun Feng

title: Spectral–Spatial Synergistic Learning and Context-Aware Edge Enhancement for Efficient Oriented Object Detection in SAR Images
content: Oriented object detection in synthetic aperture radar (SAR) imagery remains challenging because speckle noise, blurred target boundaries, strong clutter, and large-aspect-ratio objects often degrade localization accuracy and increase false alarms. Existing detectors frequently struggle to balance noise suppression, boundary preservation, and context modeling for reliable oriented localization. To address these issues, this article proposes an oriented SAR object detector based on spectral–spatial synergistic learning and context-aware edge enhancement. Specifically, a smoothed gradient enhancement module integrates differentiable Gaussian smoothing and Scharr gradient extraction to enhance blurred target boundaries while reducing spurious edge responses. A dual-domain denoising block jointly models spatial- and frequency-domain features through reparameterized spatial convolutions and spectral feature modulation, thereby suppressing clutter while preserving structural information. In addition, an existing large selective kernel block is incorporated to adaptively model long-range contextual dependencies for multiscale and large-aspect-ratio targets. Extensive experiments are conducted on RSAR, SSDD, and HRSID. On RSAR, the proposed method achieves 92.88% mAP$_{50}$ and 64.70% mAP$_{50:95}$ with 32.94M parameters and 14.08 frames/s on the test set. On SSDD and HRSID, it further obtains 99.1%/81.0% and 92.0%/66.6% in terms of mAP$_{50}$/mAP$_{50:95}$, respectively. Additional per-class analysis, ablation studies, hyperparameter sensitivity experiments, and failure-case visualizations demonstrate that the proposed design improves oriented localization robustness while revealing remaining limitations under extremely strong clutter, very small targets, and dense target distributions.
author: Yihui Zhan, Jincheng Li, Yuanyuan Shen, Xing Xie

title: GPU-Accelerated InSAR-BM3-D and OC-InSAR-BM3-D for Scalable Interferometric Phase Filtering
content: Nonlocal block-matching and 3-D filtering (BM3-D) methods, specifically InSAR-BM3-D and its offset-compensated variant OC-InSAR-BM3-D, achieve state-of-the-art interferometric SAR phase denoising quality but are computationally demanding, limiting their applicability to large-scale datasets. We present cuda-insar-bm3d, a publicly available GPU-accelerated implementation of both algorithms in CUDA C++ with a Python interface. The package implements 11 CUDA kernel modules covering block matching, 3-D grouping, collaborative filtering, and weighted aggregation. Validation against the original C++ CPU implementation on five simulated scenes confirms numerical consistency, with mean PSNR differences of +0.24 and +0.03 dB for InSAR-BM3-D and OC-InSAR-BM3-D, respectively, relative to the CPU baseline. Benchmarks on an NVIDIA RTX 3090 show up to 30× speedup for InSAR-BM3-D and 14× for OC-InSAR-BM3-D, with the acceleration factor increasing with image size. To make this acceleration accessible on consumer hardware, a memory-optimized pipeline reduces peak GPU usage from 60 GB to 8 GB for 2048 × 2048 images; adopting float32 precision yields an additional 1.5–4× speedup with negligible quality loss ($< $0.03 dB). Together with multi-GPU tiling, these optimizations scale to operational datasets: a dual-GPU configuration processed an 11 316 × 10 447 pixel RADARSAT-2 interferogram with InSAR-BM3D in under five minutes, reducing phase residues by more than 91%. The package is released as a publicly available Python library with a simple two-line API, making high-quality nonlocal phase denoising practical for operational InSAR workflows.
author: Lei Shao, Yilong Cheng, Yuheng Zhou, Jian Kang

title: 3-D Joint Inversion of Urban Persistent and Distributed Scatterers via SAR Tomography
content: Existing urban spaceborne synthetic aperture radar (SAR) tomography (TomoSAR) inversion methods predominantly focus on persistent scatterer (PS), while distributed scatterer (DS) constitute a substantial proportion of urban targets and provide critical complementary information for comprehensive urban inversion. To synergize PS and DS observations under limited data acquisition constraints, this study proposes a novel TomoSAR three-dimensional inversion framework for urban multiscattering targets. The framework establishes a three-tier network architecture: the reference network (RN), star network, and DS network. For RN construction, we propose a novel efficient and robust method, namely the directed minimum spanning tree RN. Meanwhile, to accommodate different practical requirements, two strategies for selecting construction targets are provided: one is to construct the RN using only PS, with DS appearing exclusively in the DS network; the other is to jointly construct the RN using PS and a subset of DS with relatively stable scattering properties and located in sparsely distributed PS regions. In the experimental validation, we present, for the first time, three-dimensional inversion results from joint PS and DS processing using 4-day repeat-pass LuTan-1 data over Shanghai, China.
author: Youjun Wang, Zhen Dong, Xiantao Wang, Yanyang Liu, Yucheng Gao, Anxi Yu, Yifei Ji

title: CIENet: Cross-Dimensional Information Enhancement Network for Semantic Change Detection of Desert Remote Sensing Images
content: Deserts are the driest ecosystems on Earth, with land desertification posing significant challenges to the sustainable development of inland ecological environments and human activities. However, land cover in desert regions is complex, yet sparsely distributed, and there is a lack of publicly available datasets to study desert reclamation. On the other hand, deep learning-based semantic change detection (SCD) algorithms are of critical importance for monitoring and evaluating desert reclamation. Consequently, we create a desert semantic change detection (DSCD) dataset, which contains 10 000 pairs of high-resolution remote sensing images from the northwest region of the Three-North Shelterbelt Forest, covering four distinct land cover change classes. We then propose a cross-dimensional information enhancement network (CIENet) to achieve cross-dimensional fusion of high-level semantic information and low-level spatial information for high-precision DSCD. The CIENet is capable of employing any backbone for the extraction of remote sensing features. In CIENet, Cross Dimensional Feature Fusion (CDFF) is designed to utilize high-level information to strengthen the semantic features of low-level spatial information, thereby obtaining multidimensional semantic features. Bitemporal difference information aggregation is designed to integrate independent bitemporal features to obtain a different feature. Parallel semantic information enhancement is designed to reinforce semantic features by integrating both global and local information, thereby obtaining fine-grained semantic features. Experimental results demonstrate that the proposed CIENet surpasses SOTA methods in accuracy, detail preservation, and robustness, providing a scientific foundation to assess and guide SCD.
author: Junqing Huang, Junqi Bao, Shucheng Ji, Min Xia, Xiaochen Yuan

title: Comprehensive Evaluation of the CYGNSS V3.2 Soil Moisture Product
content: The Cyclone Global Navigation Satellite System (CYGNSS) mission offers a novel capability for global soil moisture (SM) monitoring using spaceborne GNSS reflectometry with high temporal revisit and all-weather observation capability. This study presents a comprehensive evaluation of the CYGNSS V3.2 SM product over a seven-year record (Aug 2018–Dec 2024). The contributions are as follows. First, an end-to-end evaluation of the V3.2 SM product against SMAP, ISMN in-situ networks, and its legacy V1.0 product using statistical metrics and Triple Collocation. Second, a quantitative linkage between specific Level-0/Level-1 engineering calibration upgrades and measurable improvements in Level-3 SM accuracy and temporal stability. Third, a seven-year characterization of how retrieval performance is jointly impacted by land-surface homogeneity, inland waterbody, and vegetation phenology. Finally, a temporal split-sample diagnostic tool to evaluate retrieval stability, identifying retrieval limitations in regimes with sparse training data, weak reflectivity/SM sensitivity, and limited moisture dynamic range. These findings highlight both the advances achieved with CYGNSS V3.2 and the inherent challenges shared by all SM retrievals based on spaceborne GNSS-R systems. They also provide insight into future potential improvements, such as dynamic water masking, vegetation-aware modeling, and split-sample stability diagnostics for the next-generation retrieval algorithms.
author: Dinan Bai, Anthony Russel, Christopher S. Ruf

title: Cross-View Change Detection via Self-Supervised Learning
content: This article addresses the problem of cross-view heterogeneous change detection using satellite images and autonomous aerial vehicle imagery, a setting characterized by severe viewpoint differences, scale variations, and sensing modality discrepancies, as well as the absence of reliable labels. To overcome these challenges, we propose a self-supervised contrastive and predictive learning framework that learns discriminative representations directly from unlabeled cross-view image pairs. The framework jointly exploits patch-level and pixel-level objectives to capture both fine-grained local changes and higher-level semantic consistency across views. In addition, a CutMix-based data augmentation strategy is introduced to improve representation diversity. We further enhance Swin Transformer with cross-attention and channel attention mechanisms to facilitate effective multiscale and cross-modal feature interaction. Experimental results on cross-view and bitemporal change detection datasets demonstrate that the proposed approach achieves robust and competitive performance without relying on precise geometric alignment or manual annotations, highlighting its practical relevance for real-world Earth observation applications involving heterogeneous and rapidly acquired data.
author: Ghassen Graja, Olfa Besbes, Takoua Abdellatif

title: Edge Integrity Learning for Remote Sensing Image Change Detection
content: In remote sensing (RS) image change detection (CD), edge information provides critical cues for precise detection results and enhances CD performance. However, due to the susceptibility of ground object imaging to seasonal variations, weather conditions and illumination changes, change edges are prone to blending with the background, leading to insufficient utilization of information and false changes. To address this issue, we propose the Edge Integrity Learning Network (EILNet), a novel framework specifically designed for remote sensing change detection (RSCD). First, we construct a change-siamese extraction framework with edge-region decoupled representation to separately learn change edges and regions, thereby improving the accuracy of edge characterization. Then, an explicit edge focus constraint is designed to optimize edge prior learning, where an attention focusing mechanism efficiently aggregates multiscale edge features to enhance edge discrimination accuracy. Furthermore, an implicit hierarchical attention constraint is introduced to facilitate structural information exchange between change regions and edges, refining ambiguous edges. Specifically, hierarchical attention is employed to decouple change foregrounds and backgrounds by guiding multiscale change feature learning with predicted edges, thereby improving change representation performance. In addition, prior edge spatial constraints are leveraged to implicitly learn challenging samples in edge-blurred regions, further suppressing false changes. Experimental results demonstrate that our proposed method significantly improves edge discrimination accuracy in CD, outperforming state-of-the-art approaches across three public benchmarks while effectively extracting and utilizing change-related edge information.
author: Ying Wang, Yuxi Su, Zhibin Wang, Yongxiang Yao, Wei Yang, Xinghua Li

title: From Phase to Current: A Unified Error Framework for Dual-Beam ATI-SAR Ocean Current Retrieval
content: Dual-beam along-track interferometric synthetic aperture radar (DBATI-SAR) is a promising technique for retrieving two-dimensional ocean surface currents from two squinted radial-velocity observations. Its retrieval accuracy, however, is affected by heterogeneous error sources arising from wind-field uncertainty, geolocation offsets, beam- and attitude-control deviations, projection-geometry perturbations, and random phase noise. This article develops a unified joint-error modeling framework to describe how these perturbations propagate from the phase and radial-velocity domains into the retrieved current-vector domain. Analytical expressions are derived for the individual error terms and their combined propagation, providing a consistent basis for mission-level performance assessment and tolerance allocation. Full-chain simulations using representative Ku-band DBATI-SAR parameters show that the proposed model can predict retrieval errors under simultaneous multisource perturbations. The results indicate that wind-field uncertainty and attitude-induced cross-track residuals are the dominant contributors, whereas geolocation errors, projection-matrix perturbations, and random phase noise are generally secondary under the considered configurations. A real-data consistency assessment using DBATI-SAR measurements acquired over the Chudao coastal test site near Weihai, China, together with CMEMS and HYCOM reference fields, further supports the physical plausibility of the modeled error range under practical observation conditions. Overall, the developed framework can provide quantitative accuracy constraints and tolerance indicators for DBATI-SAR system design, offering theoretical support for future spaceborne ocean-current observation missions.
author: Qingyuan Shen, Tao Lai, Yuting Zhu, Bo Pan, Zixin Xie, Zhifeng Xie, Xiaoqing Wang

title: TLSPGM: A Phase-Gradient-Based Approach for Efficient 3-D Repositioning Error Compensation in D-GBSAR Slow Deformation Monitoring
content: Continuous ground-based synthetic aperture radar (C-GBSAR) suffers from heavy data loads, inflexible installation, and high costs, limiting its efficiency and maintainability. In contrast, discontinuous GBSAR (D-GBSAR) serves as a complementary technique applied more flexibly and efficiently across diverse deformation monitoring scenarios. However, its application is hindered by repositioning error compensation, as conventional methods rely on error-prone 2-D phase unwrapping that compromises both accuracy and computational efficiency. To address these challenges, this article proposes Trigonometric Least Squares Phase Gradient Method (TLSPGM), which reformulates wrapped phase into unwrapped gradient phase, enabling direct repositioning error estimation via least squares without phase unwrapping. This avoids unwrapping-induced errors and overcomes the multiextremum nonconvex optimization problem of maximum likelihood estimation. Comparative analysis shows that for signal-to-noise ratio $>$ 2 dB, TLSPGM achieves significantly higher computational efficiency than maximum likelihood method and outperforms conventional least-squares methods in compensation accuracy. Integrated into PS-InSAR, TLSPGM enables a high-precision, high-efficiency D-GBSAR monitoring framework, with its superiority in both accuracy and efficiency validated by real experiments and total station.
author: Yuanhui Mo, Tao Lai, Zhihua Zhou, Yang Yang, Wu Chen, Xiaohong Yan, Jianxun Yang, Qingsong Wang, Haifeng Huang

title: Multiview GCN-CNN Fusion Network Using Preclustering Pseudosamples for Semisupervised Hyperspectral Classification
content: Convolutional neural networks (CNNs) and graph convolutional networks (GCNs) have made significant advances in hyperspectral image (HSI) classification. However, the outstanding performance of these methods largely depends on a substantial amount of labeled samples, while the high labeling cost of HSIs leads to a scarcity of labeled samples. Meanwhile, using only CNN or GCN may result in information loss due to the limited range of feature perception, making it difficult to conduct sufficient feature mining. In this article, we propose a semisupervised HSI classification method called pseudosample guided multiview GCN-CNN fusion network (PS-MGCFN), which utilizes a pseudosample guided multiview GCN-CNN fusion network. Specifically, an adaptive center comparison pre-encoding criterion is first devised to learn to differentiate category-specific sample features and preliminarily filter valuable unlabeled samples. Furthermore, the pseudosample generation is performed by referencing the distribution characteristics of labeled samples. Then, a multiview GCN-CNN fusion network is developed to combine information from both short-range and long-range scenes for resulting in representative fusion features. Importantly, the collaborative training of a large number of pseudosamples with a small number of labeled samples greatly enhances the performance of the model. Extensive experiments conducted on three datasets demonstrate that the proposed PS-MGCFN exhibits superior stability and classification performance compared to existing methods with limited training samples.

title: Proactive Road Safety Intervention in Australia: Predicting Risky Driving Hotspots from Connected Vehicle Data
content:
arXiv:2608.16913v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Road safety monitoring has historically been reactive, relying on crash-record analysis after fatalities and injuries have already occurred. Proactive identification of high-risk locations and dangerous driving behaviour before incidents occur is a critical but underexplored challenge. This paper addresses this gap using connected vehicle telemetry data from Greater Sydney, Australia, to detect and forecast near-miss risky driving events at the Local Government Area (LGA) level. Risky driving is quantified through g-force thresholds (hard braking >0.6g, harsh cornering >0.47g, harsh acceleration >0.5g), and spatio-temporal heatmaps are constructed to identify high-risk zones. Eight predictive models are benchmarked across three families: ensemble learning (Random Forests, XGBoost, LightGBM), deep learning (LSTM, N-BEATS), and classical time-series methods (ARIMA, Exponential Smoothing, Prophet). ARIMA achieves the lowest mean absolute error (MAE: 162.21), performing comparably to LSTM (MAE: 163.92) and outperforming all ensemble methods, with N-BEATS reaching an MAE of 180.75. These results demonstrate that parsimonious time-series models are competitive with deep learning approaches when training data volume is limited. The study highlights the potential of IoT-based connected vehicle data to support proactive road safety interventions, with Sydney's inner and western LGAs (CBD, Parramatta, Bankstown) identified as persistent high-risk zones warranting targeted policy action.
author: Adriana-Simona Mih\u{a}i\c{t}\u{a}, Clarence Cheung, Artur Grigorev, Tuo Mao, David Lillo-Trynes

title: Detecting and Discriminating Operator Misspecification in Hybrid PDE-Parameter Learning: a Reference-Free Instrument, with Discrimination Bounded In Sample
content:
arXiv:2608.16925v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: We build an instrument that reads, from a single fit and with no oracle, whether the operator a hybrid PDE-parameter estimator postulates is wrong-and separates that from a merely unidentifiable parameter. On one self-adjoint parabolic inverse problem, an information-matrix statistic with plug-in scale and per-seed parameter has median 0.19 under correct specification, rejection rate $0.033$ against a pre-registered ceiling of $0.10$, and rises to $224$ and $85$ under two misspecifications, firing in every replicate. On a correctly specified but non-identifiable design it stays mute-$0.050$ at $n=200$, Clopper-Pearson $[0.024, 0.090]$-while a rank statistic collapses to zero at a pre-registered boundary $c_5^*=2.15\times10^{-3}.$ Two readings of one fit therefore separate the two failures across the three designs a deployable test reaches. That separation is the contribution; detection alone is a crowded flank. In sample it is a bound, out of sample a direction. It is needed because the usual accuracy check is blind: the misspecified estimator's in-domain RMSE is $2.7\times 10^{-2}$, below the observation noise for $\sigma\geq 0.05,$ while the coefficient is wrong by $29.7\%$ at zero noise, $31.2\%$ at the loudest. Nor is the failure architectural: a one-parameter curve fit, a bare parameter and multilayer perceptrons of $49$ and $241$ parameters converge to the same pseudo-true, matched in closed form to $0.07\%,$ whereas a physics-informed network, with its composite objective, converges to a disjoint one. We report where the instrument is blind, a pre-registered negative where a neural estimator loses to Tikhonov-regularized inversion at recovery, and the hypothesis under which its guarantee holds but a trained network violates it.
author: Eric Fock

title: Data-DPO: Direct Preference Optimization for Target Model Data Selection in LLM Post-Training
content:
arXiv:2608.16926v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Data selection in supervised fine-tuning aims to select a small set of effective samples from large-scale candidate data, reducing training cost while preserving model performance. However, existing methods usually treat data value as a relatively static property, and pay limited attention to the compatibility between data and the capability distribution of the target model. To address this issue, we propose Data-DPO, a target model-oriented SFT data selection method. Data-DPO observes the local training feedback of the target model on different samples through one-step probing, transforms activation differences among samples into pairwise data preferences, and trains a lightweight reward model to learn target-model-aware data preferences. In the final selection stage, Data-DPO further combines target model preference, external quality scores, and marginal diversity to construct a more stable and effective training subset. Experimental results on Vision-Flan and LLaVA-CoT show that Data-DPO consistently outperforms existing data selection baselines under multiple data budgets and stably surpasses full data training performance.
author: Peng Sun, Yi Yang, Antong Zhang, Chunxiao Li, Yanbo Wang, Dianbo Liu, xin chen, Kai Yu, Lu Chen, Tianfan Fu

title: Hierarchical Data Selection via Manifold Coverage and Sparse Feature Coverage in LLM Post-training
content:
arXiv:2608.16927v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: As supervised fine-tuning data continues to scale, selecting high-value subsets from large candidate pools is crucial for reducing training cost and improving model performance. Existing methods often measure diversity directly in the original embedding space, where geometric metrics entangle dominant semantic directions, fine-grained supervision differences, and local noise. We address this limitation by formulating data selection as a coarse-to-fine hierarchical coverage problem and propose MASS. MASS learns low-dimensional principal manifold coordinates with a dense autoencoder for coarse semantic grouping, and then performs quality-aware sparse feature coverage within each group using a TopK sparse autoencoder. Experiments on Vision Flan and LLaVA-CoT show that MASS consistently outperforms strong data selection baselines across multiple budgets, and in several settings matches or surpasses full data training with only a small subset of data.
author: Peng Sun, Yi Yang, Antong Zhang, Chunxiao Li, Yanbo Wang, Dianbo Liu, xin chen, Kai Yu, Lu Chen, Tianfan Fu

title: Benchmarking Classical and Transformer-Based Models for Document Sensitivity Classification
content:
arXiv:2608.16928v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Automatic sensitivity classification of organizational documents is a critical yet underserved problem, where the consequences of misclassification range from regulatory violations to security breaches. While AI-based approaches offer a scalable alternative to manual review, their reliability depends fundamentally on the integrity of training data. A pervasive but underreported problem in this domain is label leakage: residual classification markers embedded within document bodies that allow models to exploit surface shortcuts rather than learning genuine content-based sensitivity signals, producing performance estimates that are inflated and unreliable. This paper addresses this problem by introducing Strategic 16K, a carefully constructed, leakage-controlled corpus of 16,000 diplomatic cables sourced from the WikiLeaks Public Library of US Diplomacy (PlusD), and presents a systematic benchmark evaluating six model architectures spanning classical machine learning and transformer-based approaches. We document an extended leakage removal protocol that identifies and eliminates three categories of residual classification markers embedded within document bodies. On the clean benchmark, BERT achieves the strongest performance (Accuracy = 89.14%, F1 = 89.33%), followed by ELECTRA (Accuracy = 88.57%, F1 = 88.90%). Among classical models, TF-IDF with Logistic Regression achieves the strongest performance at significantly lower computational cost. These results constitute the first fully reproducible sensitivity classification benchmark constructed under explicit leakage-controlled conditions from WikiLeaks PlusD.
author: Aleesha Zainab, Muhammad Ahmed Khalid, Faheem Ullah Khan, Asifullah Khan

title: Mr.Dec: Daily-Scale Longitudinal Multimodal Modeling for 30-Day Readmission Prediction
content:
arXiv:2608.16929v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Predicting 30-day hospital readmission is essential for assessing patient stability and optimizing healthcare resources. As clinical risk evolves with the accumulation of evidence during hospitalization, capturing these dynamic trajectories is essential. However, many existing approaches compress the complex longitudinal history into fixed representations, often losing the granular, day-level clinical signals that reflect a patient's evolving physiological state. To address this, we propose Mr.Dec (Multimodal Readmission-risk prediction Decoder), which models each admission as a natural chronological sequence of daily multimodal events. By leveraging a Transformer Decoder, Mr.Dec integrates daily Electronic Health Record(EHR) updates and intermittent Chest X-ray(CXR) findings in a time-aligned stream, reflecting the actual clinical workflow. To ensure robustness, we utilize Disease-Specific Supervised Contrastive Learning as an auxiliary regularization to induce a diagnosis-aware structure in the latent space. Evaluations on the MIMIC-IV and MIMIC-CXR datasets show that Mr.Dec achieves state-of-the-art performance by preserving the integrity of the clinical sequence. Furthermore, our model identifies "Critical Days" within an admission, providing actionable and clinically grounded interpretations for real-time risk stratification. Code is available at: https://github.com/yejix-ai/MR.DEC
author: Minjun Kim, Jong Hak Moon

title: EMAN: Optimization-Driven Capacity Growth through Path Emergence in Multi-Task Learning
content:
arXiv:2608.16930v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Existing multi-task learning methods rely on hard sharing, multiple paths or experts, adaptive sharing, and dynamic expansion. However, their capacity changes are usually constrained by predefined structures or triggered by task boundaries and conflict signals.
