content: The advanced 2-D sea surface height (SSH) observations from the surface water and ocean topography (SWOT) satellite have achieved a global average geoid resolution better than 13 km, as estimated from spectral analysis of adjacent single-cycle observations. However, in regions with complex oceanic dynamics (the ocean off southwestern Argentina and east of Japan), SWOT observations show significant temporal variability across cycles. This variability greatly hampers the satellite’s ability to detect and precisely measure steady-state marine geoid signals. Even with multicycle data stacking, resolution remains poor in some regions, sometimes underperforming conventional satellite altimetry. To solve this issue, this study employs a multiresolution coherent spatio-temporal scale separation (mrCOSTS) method to analyze sea surface height anomaly (SSHA) data from 26 SWOT cycles, aiming to isolate stable signal components and reconstruct the geoid. The approach notably improves geoid resolution in regions with intricate ocean features, with the maximum enhancement reaching up to 76%. This resolution reflects the spatial scales of features reproducibly resolved by two independent SWOT geoid estimates, rather than a direct improvement in absolute marine geoid accuracy. The method effectively suppresses ocean dynamic signals while preserving the static oceanic component, and it also contributes to improving the recovery of the marine gravity field in regions characterized by complex ocean dynamics. Furthermore, in regions with relatively high resolution, the method achieves additional subtle improvements, which are of considerable significance for obtaining a stable static field.
author: Sihai Zhao, Shengjun Zhang, Xiangxue Kong, Yongjun Jia

title: A Comprehensive Statistical Framework for Identifying and Assessing Optical Marine Pseudo-Invariant Calibration Sites
content: Marine pseudo-invariant calibration sites (PICSs) support system vicarious calibration (SVC) and long-term stability monitoring of satellite ocean sensors, ensuring compliance with stringent uncertainty requirements. Significant efforts have been devoted over the past decades to identifying and characterizing PICSs. However, existing PICS assessments rely predominantly on threshold-based criteria to evaluate temporal stability, offering limited insight into the multidimensional nature of temporal stability. To address this gap, this study introduces a comprehensive framework to assess temporal stability from three complementary perspectives: 1) long-term trends in optical properties; 2) short-term (monthly scale) variability of these properties; and 3) stability of water type. The parameters of the optical properties analyzed include the diffuse attenuation coefficient at 490 nm ( $K_{d}(490)$ ), chlorophyll-a concentration ( $Chla$ ), the optical thickness of the aerosol at 869 nm ( $\tau _{a}(869)$ ) and the Angstrom exponent ( $\alpha $ ), with water type derived from the remote sensing reflectance ( $R_{rs}$ ). Long-term trends are evaluated using the Mann–Kendall test, short-term variability via threshold-based frequency analysis, and water type stability through quality assurance system (QAS) classification and frequency distributions. Applied to approximately 20 years of MODIS-Aqua Level-3 data, the framework confirms that widely recognized oceanic regions—including the North and South Pacific, North and South Atlantic, and the central Indian Ocean—exhibit high temporal stability, confirming the continued suitability of the marine optical buoy (MOBY) region as a highly stable reference site. Although our results support the suitability of several previously identified regions, they also reveal that others may not meet the PICS criteria. Rather than merely recommending specific regions, this study introduces a generalizable framework for multidimensional and objective evaluation of temporal stability, offering a scalable tool to identify and assess PICS for enhanced sensor intercalibration and long-term climate data records (CDRs) continuity in ocean color remote sensing.
author: Wenkai Li, Hongmei Zhao, Jian Li, Xi Chen, Yichu Xu, Liqiao Tian, Shilin Tang, Ling Sun

title: Assessing Conformal Prediction for Remote Sensing: Application to Local Climate Zone Classification
content: While neural networks are at the forefront of solving a variety of tasks in remote sensing, these black-box models often lack a clear sense of uncertainty. Currently experiencing a rebirth in the light of deep learning is the statistically founded uncertainty framework of conformal prediction (CP). Under certain weak assumptions, this framework provides theoretical coverage guarantees for the ground-truth value or class. The coverage guarantee holds for the predictions of the CP framework, which take the form of a prediction set containing one or more classes for classification or segmentation problems, or a prediction interval in the case of regression problems. Additionally, the size of the prediction set or interval also serves as an intuitive indicator of uncertainty. We investigate this uncertainty framework for a large-scale land cover classification dataset termed So2Sat LCZ42, which comes with ten independent expert annotations per annotated satellite image patch. We limit ourselves to the building classes of the dataset, which yield the largest proportion of expert uncertainty. The multiple annotations are here encoded into a soft label used for label uncertainty-aware training. First, we evaluate different adaptations of CP calibration methods. Next to the analysis of coverage and prediction set sizes, as a novelty, we also evaluate the methods with respect to the explainability of the conformalizer’s uncertainty toward aleatoric and epistemic uncertainty. Additionally, we construct a novel active learning (AL) framework based on CP prediction sets and show promising results in terms of expressiveness regarding predictive uncertainty. CP-based AL achieves better test performance than random querying, and yields lower predictive uncertainties than the model trained on the full training set while upholding balanced test accuracy, with only a fraction of the data needed.
author: Christoph Schweden, Peter Jung, Xiao Xiang Zhu

title: Exploratory Q-Network: A DRL Framework for MOP-Based GB-SAR Deployment in Open-Pit Coal Mine Slope Monitoring
content: Optimal ground-based synthetic aperture radar (GB-SAR) deployment is essential for high-precision slope monitoring in open-pit mines. Existing studies typically formulate GB-SAR deployment as a multiobjective optimization problem (MOP) solved by deep reinforcement learning (DRL). However, these approaches are prone to local optima in high-dimensional spaces due to three limitations: 1) the random exploration of conventional  $\epsilon $ -greedy strategies is inefficient for discovering experiences with higher rewards; 2) purely objective-driven rewards fail to motivate novel state exploration; and 3) gradient dilution in high-dimensional action spaces impedes stable convergence. To overcome these challenges, we propose the exploratory Q-network (EQN). It incorporates three components: 1) a multihead action confluence (MHAC) module that decomposes and dynamically aggregates action advantages; 2) state uncertainty rewards (SURs) with an anti-forgetting design to escape local optima and mitigate forgetting; and 3) policy perturbation factors (PPFs) that adopt NoisyNet-style perturbations to steer exploration toward higher reward paths. Multiperiod experiments at an open-pit coal mine demonstrate the efficacy of EQN, achieving 80.09% coverage and 74.95% coherence. At a 6-m resolution, EQN improves coherence by 6.16% and 12.39% and coverage by 1.34% and 19.13% when compared to the double dueling deep Q-network (D3QN) and Nondominated Sorting Genetic Algorithm II (NSGA-II), respectively.
author: Weiming Li, Zhiqiang Du, Heng Zhang

title: RS-Claw: Progressive Active Tool Exploration via Hierarchical Skill Trees for Remote Sensing Agents
content: The rise of multimodal large language models (MLLMs) led remote sensing (RS) intelligence to a new paradigm shift, i.e., from “see” to “action,” especially OpenClaw-style frameworks, which are designed to autonomously operate massive RS image processing tools to execute complex tasks. Existing RS agents adopt a passive selection paradigm for tool invocation, relying on either full tool registration (Flat) or retrieval-augmented generation (RAG). However, when confronted with the massive and multisource heterogeneous RS tool ecosystem, such passive mechanisms struggle to dynamically balance “context load” and “toolset completeness” throughout the task reasoning process, thus exhibiting inherent limitations: full tool registration triggers context space deficits during long-horizon tasks, whereas RAG retrieval leads to the omission of critical tools in essential steps. To overcome these bottlenecks, this article redefines the tool selection paradigm—arguing that the agent should act as an active explorer within the tool space. Based on this perspective, we propose RS-Claw, a novel RS agent architecture. By leveraging Skill encapsulation technology at the tool end, this architecture hierarchically structures tool descriptions, enabling the agent to execute on-demand sequential decision-making: initially selecting relevant skill branches by reading only tool summaries, then dynamically loading and reading detailed descriptions, and ultimately achieving precise invocation. This active paradigm not only reduces the context load on the agent but also effectively ensures the accurate hit rate of critical tools during long-horizon reasoning. Systematic experiments on the Earth-Bench benchmark demonstrate that RS-Claw’s active exploration mechanism effectively filters semantic noise and substantially frees up reasoning space (achieving an input token compression ratio of up to 86%), outperforming existing Flat and RAG baselines on the reported benchmark metrics.
author: Liangtian Liu, Zeyuan Wang, Ziyu Li, Kai Ouyang, Zichao Tang, Chengfu Liu, Haifeng Li, Hanwen Yu, Wentao Yang, Cheng Yang, Dongyang Hou

title: A Spatial–Spectral Denoising Algorithm for Accurate Temperature and Emissivity Retrieval From Airborne Thermal Infrared Hyperspectral Data
content: Airborne thermal infrared (TIR) hyperspectral data, with high spatial and spectral resolutions, enable the precise retrieval of land surface temperature (LST) and land surface emissivity (LSE) data for environmental monitoring and natural resource surveys. However, these sensors often suffer from increased noise due to platform and instrument factors. This study proposes an innovative spatial–spectral denoising algorithm for accurate temperature and emissivity retrieval (SSDATER), which includes: 1) applying unsupervised classification and spatial aggregation to the at-sensor radiance to reduce noise and using the emissivity spectral smoothness-constrained (ESSC) algorithm to estimate precise atmospheric parameters based on spatially aggregated observational data and 2) performing spectral aggregation on the at-sensor radiance to reduce noise. The spectrally aggregated data are then atmospherically corrected on the basis of the previously estimated atmospheric parameters, and finally, the temperature and emissivity separation (TES) algorithm is employed to retrieve accurate LST&E values. Assuming that autocorrelation exists in the LSE spectrum, principal component analysis (PCA)-based regression is used to convert the retrieved multispectral LSE into hyperspectral LSE. The SSDATER method was evaluated on simulated airborne Hyper-CAM LW data. The results show that the atmospheric parameters estimated by the SSDATER method were more accurate than those estimated from Hyper-CAM LW data using the ESSC algorithm and those simulated directly from reanalysis atmospheric profiles using the radiative transfer model. When identical atmospheric parameters were used, the SSDATER method achieved the highest accuracy for LST&E retrieval (LST RMSE: 1.01 K and average LSE RMSE: 0.016), thus outperforming the TES algorithm on original Hyper-CAM LW data (LST RMSE: 1.91 K and average LSE RMSE: 0.036). In summary, the proposed SSDATER method demonstrates the potential for high-precision LST&E retrieval from noisy airborne TIR hyperspectral data within a simulation-based validation framework, thereby supporting further application studies with real airborne observations.
author: Shugui Zhou, Fawang Ye, Jie Cheng

title: MICS-Net: Manifold-Regularized and Intrinsically Constrained Dual- to Quad-Pol SAR Reconstruction for HJ-2E/F Satellites
content: China’s S-band HJ-2E/F synthetic aperture radar (SAR) constellation offers great potential for ecological monitoring, but its primary dual-polarimetric (DP) mode suffers from scattering ambiguity. Reconstructing quad-polarimetric (QP) data from underdetermined DP observations is crucial to overcoming this. However, this inverse problem requires balancing physical validity of covariance matrices with high-fidelity polarimetric statistics. To address limitations of existing deep learning methods, including weak physical constraints, metric distortion, and poor terrain prior usage, we propose MICS-Net, a manifold-regularized and intrinsically constrained SAR reconstruction network (MICS-Net). It integrates three core components: a Schur-complement-based intrinsic constraint layer for positive semidefinite (PSD) guarantees, a Riemannian manifold synergistic loss (RMSL) for preserving scattering topology, and a dual-stream sensing terrain-driven module (DS-TDM) incorporating spatial priors to compensate for topographic distortions. Experiments show that MICS-Net achieves 100% physically valid reconstruction, reducing average Wishart distance by 6.28% compared with state-of-the-art methods. In wetland detection, reconstructed QP data improve overall accuracy (OA) by up to 4.4% over DP observations. Results confirm that embedding physical rules and manifold constraints into neural networks is essential for high-fidelity reconstruction for reliable ecological monitoring applications.
author: Shun Lu, Hong Zhang, Yue Ren, Zihuan Guo, Nanhuanuowa Zhu, Xiaoling Bi, Yuhao Xie, Honglei Yang

title: Differential Dual-Channel 1-bit SAR Imaging Based on Single-Frequency Time-Varying Threshold
content: 1-bit quantization can alleviate the data burden of synthetic aperture radar (SAR) on resource-constrained platforms but suffers from severe nonlinear distortion. To overcome the existing 1-bit methods’ reliance on high-frequency hardware and high oversampling rates, as well as the inability of Coupled 2-bit schemes to recover relative amplitude, this article proposes a differential dual-channel 1-bit SAR imaging method based on a single-frequency threshold (SFT) strategy and phase modulation. By feeding the analog echo into a dual-channel differential architecture with a  $\pi $  phase inversion in one branch, it structurally eliminates all the single-frequency interference components and the dominant intermodulation components. Requiring only low-cost xor logic, this approach achieves effective suppression of the dominant interference components and spectral separation at a threefold oversampling rate under the adopted parameter design. Theoretical and experimental results demonstrate that it effectively preserves relative amplitude relationships in multitarget scenes and significantly suppresses the quantization noise floor, providing a high-fidelity lightweight paradigm for small platforms.
author: Shiqi Liu, Yihang Ai, Bing Li, Bo Zhao, Lei Huang, Hing Cheung So

title: SSH-Net: Symplectic-Inspired Discrete Dynamic Evolution for Hyperspectral Image Classification
content: Hyperspectral image classification (HSIC) relies on effective modeling of coupled spectral–spatial interactions. While recent CNN-, Transformer-, and Mamba-based methods have improved feature extraction, most of them organize token interaction through layerwise aggregation and repeated stacking, leaving cross-layer propagation only implicitly modeled. To address this issue, we propose SSH-Net, a symplectic-inspired spectral–spatial dynamic interaction network for HSIC. The proposed framework parameterizes token representations as latent position and momentum states and performs gated leapfrog-style dynamic updates to realize structured multistep feature propagation. On top of this dynamic backbone, a terminal-state descriptor branch summarizes the final position, momentum, and interaction-response statistics as terminal-state evidence, and a discriminative evidence aggregation (DEA) branch integrates such evidence with multiscale spatial and global contextual features for prediction. In this way, SSH-Net combines Hamiltonian-inspired dynamic propagation with complementary state-aware readout for hyperspectral classification. Experiments on four public benchmarks, namely Indian Pines, Houston2013, WHU-Hi-LongKou, and WHU-Hi-HanChuan, show that SSH-Net achieves consistently competitive or superior performance in terms of overall accuracy (OA), average accuracy (AA), and kappa coefficient compared with representative baseline methods. These results suggest that symplectic-inspired dynamic propagation provides a useful inductive bias for organizing spectral–spatial interaction in HSIC. Codes are available at https://github.com/yi1275174812/SSH-Net
author: Zihang Luo, Xiaofei Yang, Fei Yu, Waixi Liu, Yifang Ban, Yicong Zhou

title: DBSSM: A Dual-Branch Spectral–Spatial Mamba Network for Hyperspectral Image Classification
content: Hyperspectral image (HSI) classification has been widely applied in numerous fields. Although deep learning-based methods have improved classification performance, existing approaches still struggle to balance accuracy and computational efficiency. Convolutional neural network (CNN)-based methods are limited by local receptive fields, whereas Transformer-based methods suffer from high computational complexity, restricting their application in large-scale scenarios. To achieve collaborative optimization of classification accuracy and computational efficiency, a dual-branch spectral–spatial Mamba (DBSSM) network is proposed, which employs a dual-branch architecture with an interactive feature fusion strategy for efficient joint spectral–spatial modeling. The main contributions are as follows: 1) a spatial dual-scan Mamba (SDSM) module is developed to extract rich sequential features via a dual-directional scanning strategy and shared mechanism, enabling long-range dependency modeling with relatively low computational complexity; 2) a spectral group attention (SGA) module is designed to reduce the number of parameters via a grouping strategy while enhancing spectral information interaction using a self-attention mechanism; and 3) an interactive attention fusion module (IAFM) is proposed to achieve bidirectional interactive fusion between spatial and spectral features, thereby further enhancing the feature learning capability. Experimental results on four benchmark hyperspectral datasets demonstrate that DBSSM outperforms state-of-the-art methods in classification performance while maintaining a low parameter count and computational cost, validating its effectiveness. The code is available at https://github.com/Present-Li/DBSSM
author: Hanzhong Li, Hua Huang, Hongfeng Li, Jiangtao Peng, Bengong Zhang, Yazhou Shi, Huizhen Li

title: Potential Energy-Constrained Quantum Hybrid Attention Network for Hyperspectral Anomaly Detection
content: Hyperspectral anomaly detection (HAD) aims to identify pixels that differ from complex background distributions without prior target information. Deep learning methods such as convolutional neural networks (CNNs) and transformers have been widely investigated for HAD. However, complex nonlinear spectral relationships in highly mixed backgrounds remain difficult to characterize. Meanwhile, without prior information, training may lack guidance for separating backgrounds and anomalies, weakening anomaly–background separability and causing anomaly contamination. To address these issues, in this article, a potential energy-constrained quantum hybrid attention network (PEQA) is proposed for HAD with three key modules. Specifically, the quantum spectral–spatial attention (QSA) module embeds a quantum neural network (QNN) into the spectral attention branch, where spectral features are encoded into quantum states and channelwise similarity is measured by quantum fidelity, enabling nonlinear spectral interactions to be captured within the attention process. Moreover, the potential energy (PE) loss constrains bottleneck features from an energy-distribution perspective, allowing dense background-dominated latent regions to have lower potential values while making relatively isolated anomaly related samples more distinguishable. Finally, the background prior guidance (BPG) module provides auxiliary background guidance, with superpixel segmentation first generating locally homogeneous regions and singular value decomposition (SVD) extracting dominant components for background prior construction. The experimental results on six datasets indicate that PEQA achieves favorable detection performance compared with nine representative HAD methods.
author: Xingzhi Du, Shou Feng, Peiyi Zhang, Nan Su, Chunhui Zhao

title: Self-Supervised Hyperspectral Super-Resolution From RGB With Score-Distilled Spectral Prior
content: Recovering hyperspectral images (HSIs) from RGB observations is a highly ill-posed problem due to severe spectral information loss. However, current methods either rely on costly paired RGB–HSI datasets that are difficult to obtain or on unpaired RGB–HSI data for spectral guidance, which increases training costs and often leads to physically distorted spectral reconstructions. To address these challenges, we propose a self-supervised score-distilled spectral prior (SDSP) framework, which consists of a wavelet-based cross-attention reconstruction network (WCAR-Net) as the generator and a pretrained spectral diffusion model as the data-driven spectral expert. Score distillation sampling (SDS) is applied to the diffusion model to compute spectral gradients, which are incorporated into the generator’s loss to iteratively refine its predictions and produce high-quality hyperspectral reconstructions. In WCAR-Net, a cross-attention refinement module is designed to fuse spatial details with high-level semantic features, while wavelet-based feature decomposition preserves fine frequency-domain structures. Guided by the spectral expert provided by the diffusion model, the network is trained in a self-supervised and iterative manner, thereby eliminating the need for paired RGB–HSI data. Extensive experiments on multiple datasets demonstrate that our method significantly outperforms state-of-the-art approaches in both spectral fidelity and spatial reconstruction.
author: Ningjia Lv, Feiwang Yuan, Wei He, Qiangqiang Zhou, Jinshan Zeng, Yong Chen

title: Memory-Efficient 3-D RTM Using Low-Rank Adaptive Compressed SVD Based on Single-Layer Boundary Saving and Nyquist Sampling
content: The massive memory requirements of the source wavefield reconstruction (SWR) in GPU-accelerated 3-D elastic reverse time migration (ERTM) severely limit practical large-scale geological imaging. To address this bottleneck, this study proposes a boundary wavefield compression method integrating the single-layer boundary saving method (S-BSM), Nyquist sampling, and a CUDA-accelerated low-rank adaptive compressed singular value decomposition (LoRA-cSVD) algorithm. Three key innovations are introduced: 1) Nyquist-sampled single-layer BSM (NS-BSM), which combines SBSM with Nyquist sampling to generate lightweight 2-D single-layer boundary wavefield data for compressed SVD (cSVD) compression, 2) using the singular value matrix of cSVD to adaptively determine the compression rank under a predefined energy loss ratio, and 3) dynamically adjusting the calculation rank of cSVD based on the compression rank from the previous time step. Numerical results demonstrate that LoRA-cSVD compresses boundary wavefield data by  $\approx$ 10-fold to the megabyte scale versus NS-BSM, with a mere  $\approx$ 6% increase in computational time compared to standalone forward simulation. The compressed boundary wavefield data can fully reside in video RAM (VRAM), eliminating redundant memory copying and outperforming S-BSM by  $\approx$ 7% in overall computational efficiency. This study provides a practical, memory-efficient solution for large-scale, 3-D geological imaging while maintaining high imaging accuracy.
author: Wei Cai, Peimin Zhu, Ziang Li

title: Full-Waveform Inversion for Defect Detection in Earth-Rock Dams Based on a Quasi-Crosswell Acquisition Geometry
content: When seismic methods are employed to detect latent defects in Earth-rock dams, conventional acquisition geometries with receivers deployed along the longitudinal profile of the dam acquire limited wavefield information associated with defect zones, thereby restricting the accuracy of defect inversion. Considering the actual structural characteristics of dams, a full-waveform inversion (FWI) scheme based on a quasi-crosswell acquisition geometry is proposed for the detection of dam defects, where the spatial location and velocity characteristics of defect zones are inverted using seismic data acquired along the transverse profile of the dam. The quasi-crosswell acquisition geometry enables the recording of not only direct P-waves (DPs) and S-waves (DSs) traversing the dam but also multiple reflections associated with defect zones generated from the free surfaces of the dam, which provide better illumination for the defect zones within the dam. The results indicate that the key wavefields determining the inversion accuracy of dam defects include direct waves traversing the dam and reflected waves from both the bedrock interface and dam slopes, whereas the contribution of reflections from the defect zones is minimal. To improve the stability and accuracy of the inversion, a preconditioning operator suitable for quasi-crosswell seismic data inversion is constructed, with an optimized parabolic fitting method calculating the inversion step length. Through multiscale FWI of dam models with typical defects, the proposed method is validated for effectively constructing high-precision velocity models for Earth-rock dams.
author: Hao Xu, Fei Cheng, Daicheng Peng, Jiangping Liu, Zhuo Fan

title: Enhancing Electrical Resistivity Tomography Detection of Landslide Structures Through Multisource Geological Constraints
content: The electrical resistivity tomography (ERT) method is a powerful tool for inferring subsurface structures in landslide investigations. However, its effectiveness is often limited by the inherent nonuniqueness of inversion and the severe smearing artifacts caused by conventional regularization, particularly for delineating thin structures like slip zones. To address these challenges, this article proposes a unified and application-oriented constrained inversion framework for ERT that flexibly integrates multisource prior geological information. Building on established constrained inversion concepts, the framework combines structurally guided directional constraints, borehole resistivity constraints, differentiated regional constraints, and localized borehole-derived interface and dip constraints within a consistent Gauss–Newton inversion workflow. The framework integrates different types of constraints into the inversion process, including structural orientations, known resistivity points from boreholes, and predetermined interface positions. We first demonstrate the efficacy of each constraint type through numerical simulations on a theoretical landslide model. The method was then validated with a comprehensive field study at the Huangtupo landslide in the Three Gorges Reservoir area of China. In situ resistivity tests within a tunnel system provided characteristic resistivity values for key structural elements (slip zone, slip mass, and bedrock), forming the basis for the reference model. Constrained inversions were performed on four ERT survey lines by incorporating interfaces from seismic ambient noise tomography (S-ANT) and orientations from multiple boreholes and tunnels. The results show that, compared with unconstrained inversion, the proposed constrained strategy reduces inversion ambiguity associated with equivalence and suppresses the smearing effects, enabling a clearer identification of multilevel landslide structures that are typically obscured in standard ERT images. Finally, a detailed and reliable 3-D model of the landslide was constructed by integrating the interpreted 2-D profiles. The proposed constrained inversion approach mitigates the common pitfalls of standard ERT and provides a practical methodological basis for landslide characterization and stability analysis.
author: Fan Li, Kai Lu, Guangtian Niu, Peng Wang, Zhenyu Li

title: Synergistic Use of Time-Series Multispectral and Synthetic Aperture Radar Data for Adaptive Glacier Surface-State Mapping
content: Monitoring glacier surface wetness and near-surface facies evolution with high spatiotemporal resolution is important for characterizing seasonal melt conditions and supporting downstream glaciological modeling. However, current remote sensing methods are hindered by cloud contamination in optical data and ambiguities in SAR backscatter interpretation. In this study, a novel framework for automated glacier surface-state mapping is proposed by integrating Sentinel-1 SAR and Sentinel-2 optical imagery. Pixel-wise wet snow probability maps are generated using a convolutional neural network trained on multitemporal optical data, which then guides an adaptive thresholding scheme for SAR-based wet snow detection. Finally, the wet snow maps are refined through a postprocessing scheme that leverages temporal consistency and spatial segmentation, and classification stability is significantly enhanced. The proposed algorithm is evaluated over three glaciers on the Tibetan Plateau using carefully constructed remote-sensing reference labels. The results show agreement with the reference labels, with mean F1-scores of 0.849 for Shenshe Glacier, 0.811 for Laohugou Glacier No.12, and 0.858 for Bayi Glacier, with peak values exceeding 0.93 during mid-season observations. The results also indicate relatively stable agreement under varying signal conditions. This study provides a flexible and transferable strategy for mapping wet-snow extent, wet-snow timing, and glacier surface facies evolution, which can provide useful constraints for subsequent mass-balance and runoff modelling in complex mountainous terrain.
author: Zhenzhao Xing, Xin Zhou, Lingxiao Peng, Zhe Zhang, Yirong Wu

title: A Physics-Guided Machine Learning Approach for Efficient Multiparameter Retrieval of Overlapping Cloud Properties
content: Overlapping clouds (OLCs) play a critical role in Earth’s radiation budget and climate change. The accurate characterization of their properties is essential for cloud radiative effect (CRE) estimates. The existing physical retrieval methods can analytically derive properties of OLCs with optically thin ice clouds overlying water clouds, but require rigorous radiative transfer solutions, which are computationally expensive. This study proposes a retrieval framework integrating a radiative transfer model (RTM) and machine learning (ML) to facilitate the efficient and multiparameter simultaneous retrieval of OLCs with optically thin ice clouds overlying water clouds, including cloud base height (CBH), cloud top height (CTH), cloud effective radius (CER), and cloud optical thickness (COT). The visible-to-infrared observations (0.86, 1.6, 2.25, 8.6, 11, and 12 μm) from visible infrared imaging radiometer suite are used as predictors. CTH and CBH from the active sensor and RTM-derived COT and CER are utilized as reference values. Based on the data from 2017 to 2019, the physics-guided ML method is demonstrated to effectively retrieve both ice and water cloud properties in OLCs, improving predictive performance and physical consistency. Specifically, Pearson’s correlation coefficients for CBH and CTH exceed 0.85, while those for CER and COT exceed 0.90. Validated against active observations, the bias and root-mean-square error of predicted CTH (CBH) are −0.36 ± 1.79 (−0.30 ± 1.75) km for upper level thin ice clouds and −0.18 ± 1.74 (−0.27 ± 1.65) km for lower level water clouds. Moreover, the spatial and seasonal distribution characteristics of COT and CER are revealed. Overall, this approach offers efficient and reliable property retrieval of OLCs, showing potential for improving their CRE estimations.
author: Yining Yang, Shiwen Teng, Wencai Wang, Yulin Xie, Chao Liu, Lifang Sheng

title: Secure and Efficient Lossless Compression of Binary Semantic Masks for Remote Sensing via Modified 2D-DCT
content: Binary semantic masks (BSMs) represent a type of structured discrete data that describe the spatial distribution of target and background regions. As critical outputs of on-board AI processing in remote sensing, transmitting these data securely and efficiently over constrained channels poses a significant challenge, since traditional methods struggle to balance high compression ratios (CRs) with robust data protection. To address this problem, this article proposes a framework for the secure and efficient lossless compression of BSMs, named joint encryption and lossless compression framework for (JELCF)-BSM. The method first exploits spatial redundancy by segmenting the data into homogeneous blocks (HB) and non-HB, followed by encryption via block-level scrambling and diffusion. Subsequently, a modified 2-D binary discrete cosine transform is designed to establish a one-to-one correspondence between binary blocks and transform-domain DC coefficients. Based on this unique representation, an index coding strategy is developed to achieve efficient lossless compression of encrypted semantic masks. Experimental results demonstrate that JELCF-BSM achieves an average CR approximately 82% higher than conventional lossless compression schemes when compressing encrypted BSMs, and 56% higher than compared joint encryption and compression schemes. Security evaluations further confirm that the method exhibits strong robustness against statistical and differential attacks. This method provides a feasible solution for secure and efficient remote sensing semantic data transmission.
author: Xiaoran Leng, Weijia Cao, Xijun He, Xiang Zhou

title: SCC-Loc: A Unified Semantic Cascade Consensus Framework for UAV Thermal Geo-Localization
content: Cross-modal Thermal Geo-localization provides a robust, all-weather solution for Unmanned Aerial Vehicles (UAVs) in Global Navigation Satellite System-denied environments. However, profound thermal-visible modality gaps introduce severe feature ambiguity, systematically corrupting conventional coarse-to-fine registration. To address this bottleneck, we propose SCC-Loc, a unified Semantic-Cascade-Consensus localization framework. By sharing a single DINOv2 backbone across global retrieval and MINIMA$_{\text{RoMa}}$ matching, it minimizes memory footprint and achieves zero-shot, highly accurate absolute position estimation. Specifically, we tackle modality ambiguity by introducing three cohesive components. First, we design the Semantic-Guided Viewport Alignment module to adaptively optimize satellite crop regions, effectively correcting initial spatial deviations. Second, we develop the Cascaded Spatial-Adaptive Texture-Structure Filtering mechanism to explicitly enforce geometric consistency, thereby suppressing dense cross-modal outliers. Finally, we propose the Consensus-Driven Reliability-Aware Position Selection strategy to determine the optimal position by integrating physically constrained pose optimization, multidimensional reliability evaluation, and geographic consensus. To address data scarcity, we construct Thermal-UAV, a comprehensive dataset providing 11 890 diverse thermal queries referenced against a large-scale satellite ortho-photo and corresponding spatially aligned Digital Surface Model. Extensive experiments demonstrate that SCC-Loc establishes a new state-of-the-art, suppressing the mean localization error to 9.37 m and providing a 7.6-fold accuracy improvement within a strict 5-m threshold over the strongest baseline.
author: Xiaoran Zhang, Yu Liu, Jinyu Liang, Kangqiushi Li, Zhiwei Huang, Huaxin Xiao

title: STG-Net: Shared Tensor Guidance Hyperspectral and Multispectral Remote Sensing Image Fusion Network Under Locally Overlapping Condition
content: Hyperspectral image (HSI) and multispectral image (MSI) fusion aims to generate a high spatial and spectral resolution hyperspectral image (HR-HSI) by integrating the spectral information of low-resolution HSI (LR-HSI) and the spatial information of high-resolution MSI. However, most existing fusion methods are developed under the fully overlapping assumption, and their ability to exploit locally shared information becomes limited when the two modalities only cover a partially common area. In addition, directly extending the tensor representation learned from the overlapping region to nonoverlapping regions is challenging because these regions lack LR-HSI spectral observations. To overcome these issues, in this article, an unsupervised shared tensor guidance network, termed STG-Net, is proposed for HSI–MSI fusion under locally overlapping conditions. Specifically, a local-to-global deep Tucker representation is constructed to learn a shared core tensor from the reliable overlapping area. Then, a multiscale attentive core synthesizer is designed to propagate the learned core representation to the full scene by exploring multiscale spatial–spectral features. Finally, an adaptive weighted fusion reconstructor reconstructs the HR-HSI by adaptively combining the overlap-constrained reconstruction and the full-scene MSI-guided reconstruction. The whole framework is optimized without ground-truth HR-HSI by using observation-domain degradation consistency, overlap-region cross-reconstruction, style consistency, and manifold regularization. Experiments on three benchmark datasets under ×4 and ×8 downsampling settings demonstrate the effectiveness of STG-Net. On the Pavia University dataset under ×4 downsampling and 80% overlap, STG-Net achieves a peak signal-to-noise ratio of 42.50 dB.
author: Tong Gao, Yipeng Rao, Hongwei Dong, Lingyu Si, Yongqiang Sun

title: MEP: An Integrated MASH-EAGLE-PASTA Method for Extreme Class Imbalance in Marine Debris Segmentation
content: Preserving ocean ecosystems and achieving UN Sustainable Development Goal 14 require automated marine pollution surveillance. Nevertheless, marine satellite-based semantic segmentation of marine pollution faces extreme scale imbalance, with pollution classes comprising less than 0.5% of pixels relative to extensive marine water, leading to traditional algorithms showing majority-class gradient bias in training and precision-recall biases in inference. To overcome these shortcomings, this article proposes MEP, a unified model that addresses class imbalance through combined architectural, optimization, and inference-level innovations. The Multiscale Attention Swin Hamburger architecture uses a Swin Transformer encoder with shifted-window self-attention for hierarchical feature decomposition, alongside a Hamburger decoder that uses nonnegative matrix factorization to model global context. The Equal Adaptive Gradient Learning Engine automatically estimates per-batch inverse-frequency weights for classes, weighted focal loss, and class-balanced Dice loss to ensure a democratic contribution of the gradient, regardless of pixel count. During inference, Precision-Aware Selective Test-Time Augmentation combines eight geometric augmentations and applies confidence-sensitive rejection to avoid systematic overprediction without discarding actual detections. State-of-the-art results on the MADOS benchmark have been achieved, with a mean F1-score of 79.0%, a mean IoU of 69.2%, and an overall accuracy of 94.1%, representing improvements of 3.0%, 4.9%, and 5.0% over the original published MariNeXt results. The framework achieves strong performance across 14 of 15 classes, though the Foam class remains challenging due to fundamental spectral similarity with Turbid Water at the available sensor resolution. Furthermore, cross-validation on the MARIDA benchmark yielded promising results without dataset-specific tuning, confirming generalizability across marine environments.
author: Arun Kumar Sangaiah, Muhammad Luqman Arif Mohamad, Neelkanth Mawood, Yi-Bing Lin, Mohd Amiruddin Abd Rahman, Jenq-Shiou Leu

title: An Edge-Aware and Noise Resilient CNN-ViT Hybrid Network With Cross-Attention Feature Fusion for PolSAR Land Cover Classification
content: Polarimetric synthetic aperture radar (PolSAR) data is characterized by a complex high-dimensional structure and inherent speckle noise. Consequently, standalone convolutional neural network (CNN) or vision transformer (ViT) architectures struggle to simultaneously suppress noise and preserve discriminative features. In this article, a CNN–ViT hybrid network with cross-attention feature fusion is proposed for edge-aware and noise-resilient PolSAR land cover classification. First, an edge enhancement module is designed to strengthen the discriminative features of region boundaries across different land cover types in PolSAR images. Then, a lightweight residual shrinkage network with adaptive soft thresholding is proposed for the local feature learning branch. It effectively mitigates the influence of inherent speckle noise while preserving critical spatial structures. For global context modeling, a patch merged ViT module is introduced, which reduces computational redundancy and enhances feature learning by merging similar image patches. Finally, a local–global feature interaction module based on cross-attention is designed to dynamically integrate complementary features from both branches. It enables the network to fully exploit the strengths of both local texture details and global contextual information. Experimental results on four PolSAR datasets demonstrate that the proposed method achieves superior classification accuracy compared to existing approaches, effectively balancing edge preservation and noise robustness.
author: Yuechao Chen, Siyuan Wu, Meijuan Yang, Jianlong Wang, Dou Quan, Jiajia Gao

title: GLUSE: Enhanced Channelwise Adaptive Gated Linear Units SE for Onboard Satellite Earth Observation Image Classification
content: This study introduces ResNet-GLUSE, a lightweight ResNet variant enhanced with gated linear unit-enhanced squeeze-and-excitation (GLUSE), an adaptive channelwise attention mechanism. By integrating dynamic gating into the traditional SE framework, GLUSE improves feature recalibration while maintaining computational efficiency. Experiments on EuroSAT and PatternNet datasets confirm its effectiveness, achieving exceeding 94% and 98% accuracy, respectively. While MobileViT achieves 99% accuracy, ResNet-GLUSE offers 33× fewer parameters, 27× fewer FLOPs, 33× smaller model size (MB), $\approx 6\times$ lower power consumption (W), and $\approx 3\times$ faster inference time (s), making it significantly more efficient for onboard satellite deployment. Furthermore, due to its simplicity, ResNet-GLUSE can be easily mimicked for neuromorphic computing, enabling ultralow power inference at just 852.30 mW on Akida Brainchip. This balance between high accuracy and ultralow resource consumption establishes ResNet-GLUSE as a practical solution for real-time Earth observation (EO) tasks. Reproducible codes are available in our shared repository. Impact Statement– ResNet-GLUSE adds a lightweight, dynamic gated attention to a small ResNet, reaching high accuracy with a fraction of the computation, memory, and power required by existing models, enabling real-time image analytics directly on satellite edge hardware. This synergy of performance, scalability, and energy efficiency accelerates rapid decision-making in resource-constrained orbital environments, aiding critical tasks like near-real-time hazard detection and precision agriculture. Reproducible codes promote broad adoption and facilitate ongoing innovation, underscoring ResNet-GLUSE's potential as a transformative solution for next-generation EO missions.
author: Thanh-Dung Le, Vu Nguyen Ha, Ti Ti Nguyen, Duc-Dung Tran, Hung Nguyen-Kha, Luis Manuel Garces-Socarras, Juan Carlos Merlano-Duncan, Symeon Chatzinotas

title: Spatiotemporal Ambiguity-Driven System Parameter Design Method for Moon-Based SAR
content: Moon-based synthetic aperture radar (SAR) offers a vantage point for continuous, hemispheric-scale Earth observation. However, existing research primarily focuses on individual performance metrics or geometric coverage, lacking an effective system design methodology that jointly accounts for spatial coverage, timing constraints, and ambiguity performance. This article addresses the challenges of performance analysis and parameter design for Moon-based SAR. First, the spatiotemporal evolution of range and azimuth ambiguities is investigated. By incorporating the dynamic Earth–Moon geometry, this study analyzes the fluctuation amplitudes of range and azimuth ambiguities, which reach up to 18 and 11 dB, respectively, and explains their periodic degradation mechanisms. Second, an iterative framework for system parameter design and performance evaluation is proposed. This methodology addresses the complex trade-offs among system variables, establishing a pulse repetition frequency selection mechanism to enable the constrained joint selection of critical parameters such as antenna dimensions and beam position allocation. Finally, the proposed framework is validated through distinct C-band Moon-based ScanSAR design scenarios: a wide-swath mode (5000 km, 30 m resolution) and a high-resolution mode (1000 km, 3 m resolution). The evaluation of imaging metrics, including the noise equivalent sigma zero under average transmitted power constraints, demonstrates the applicability of the design method to diverse Earth observation missions.
author: Kangxin Xiong, Zhirong Men, Pengbo Wang, Wenjin Wu, Jianan Li, Yiya Tang, Jie Chen

title: ProtoMix: Unified Prototype Learning for Semantic Change Detection in Remote Sensing
content: As an emerging topic, semantic change detection (SCD) in remote sensing aims to both identify the locations of changes before and after events and determine the land cover (LC) classes of changed regions. While deep learning has demonstrated its great potential for SCD, the following two fundamental challenges remain: large variations among the same LC class as well as close similarity between different LC classes, and the severe underutilization of massive unchanged regions, which dominate remote sensing scenes but lack detailed semantic annotations. To address these issues, we propose a novel prototype learning framework for SCD, namely ProtoMix, by leveraging both labeled and unlabeled regions (i.e., unchanged regions) and exploiting interclass similarity and intraclass variation. ProtoMix functions through a Siamese encoder–decoder architecture with multitask learning for both change detection and semantic segmentation. Specifically, the framework represents each semantic class using a cluster of prototypes, capturing variations within and across classes. To leverage the rich semantics in unchanged regions, a pseudoprototype assignment strategy is devised for deriving semantic classes of unlabeled pixels with high confidence, while treating low-confidence pixels as negative samples in a contrastive learning scheme. Intuitively, by representing each class with a cluster of multiple prototypes, ProtoMix naturally accommodates high intraclass variance. Simultaneously, the contrastive learning scheme explicitly pushes prototypes of different classes apart, effectively mitigating interclass similarity. Comprehensive experiments on two widely used datasets SECOND and LANDSAT-SCD demonstrate the state-of-the-art performance of our ProtoMix proposed.
author: Hengzhi Chen, Kun Hu, Patrick Filippi, Wei Xiang, Thomas Francis Bishop, Zhiyong Wang

title: Rainfall-Induced Landslide Detection in the Central–Southern Andes of Chile Using Integrated SAR, Optical, and Machine-Learning Approaches in Google Earth Engine
content: This article presents a framework for postevent detection of rainfall-induced landslides in the south-central Andes of Chile by combining Sentinel-1 C-band synthetic aperture radar backscatter changes (∼10-m resolution), Sentinel-2 multispectral variables (10-m resolution), and advanced land observing satellite PALSAR-derived topographic attributes within a machine-learning workflow implemented in Google Earth Engine. The framework comprises three stages: 1) multisource feature extraction; 2) classification using random forest (RF), gradient tree boosting (GTB), support vector machine (SVM), classification and regression trees (CART), and Naïve Bayes (NB), evaluated through nested leave-one-area of interest-out spatial cross-validation; and 3) probability mapping. The approach was applied to landslides triggered by an extreme rainfall event between 20 and 25 June 2023, in the Andean sector of the Biobío Region. Under the reference configuration, RF achieved the best performance (F1 = 0.883, Precision = 0.947, Recall = 0.829), followed by GTB (F1 = 0.869); CART, SVM, and NB reached F1-scores of 0.825, 0.822, and 0.753, respectively. Sensitivity analyses showed strong effects of temporal sampling and optical data quality. The 7-day postevent scenario yielded spatially unreliable results (F1 = 0.463), whereas a 50-day period improved performance (F1 = 0.650). Restricting Sentinel-2 composites to the dry season improved results relative to longer periods affected by cloud and snow contamination (F1 = 0.883 versus 0.818). Overall, normalized difference vegetation index percentage change combined with RF provided the most robust performance for operational landslide probability mapping.
author: Luis Gajardo, Edilia Jaque-Castillo, Mario Lillo-Saavedra, Francisco Castro-Venegas

title: Global Ionospheric Scintillation During the May 2024 Super Geomagnetic Storm Observed by TianMu-1 GNSS-R
content: Global navigation satellite system reflectometry (GNSS-R) provides broad oceanic coverage and serves as a crucial tool for monitoring ionospheric scintillation. However, current GNSS-R constellations, such as cyclone GNSS (CYGNSS), are constrained by low orbital inclinations, limiting high-latitude observations. The TianMu-1 (TM-1) constellation, with more satellites and higher inclinations, enables global-scale monitoring. Using GNSS-R data from the TM-1 constellation, this study systematically investigates the spatiotemporal characteristics of ionospheric scintillation over global oceanic regions during the main phase of the May 2024 super geomagnetic storm. The results show that TM-1 GNSS-R-derived scintillation observations are highly consistent with those from CYGNSS, COSMIC-2, and ground-based GNSS rate of total electron content index measurements, thereby validating the capability of TM-1 to capture ionospheric scintillation signatures over oceanic regions. During the storm’s main phase, the number of scintillation events exhibited a nonmonotonic “increase–brief decline–resurgence” evolution, governed by the successive action of prompt penetration electric fields, the transition between under- and overshielding states, and the disturbance dynamo electric field. Scintillation also displayed a pronounced latitudinal dependence: high-latitude events were the most intense, longest lasting, and largest in scale; mid-latitude events were the weakest; and low-latitude events were more numerous than those at mid-latitudes but generally weaker than those at high latitudes, with pronounced clustering over the Arabian Sea and the Bay of Bengal. These results demonstrate the potential of TM-1 GNSS-R for global ionospheric scintillation monitoring during super geomagnetic storms.
author: Linghuo Jian, Xiaodong Ren, Yingchuan Yang, Xuan Le, Hang Liu, Yu Guo, Xiaohong Zhang

title: UniRS-Instruct: A Principle-Guided Unified Instruction-Following Dataset for Remote Sensing Understanding
content: Driven by multimodal large language models (MLLMs), remote sensing image (RSI) understanding is undergoing a paradigm shift, evolving from learning a domain-specific model to learning a general foundation model with domain adaptation (LaGD). Under the LaGD paradigm, conventional datasets, such as DOTA and RSICD, which fueled progress in RSI understanding over the past decade, are no longer adequate for emerging tasks because their annotation formats are task-specific and lack the language-level supervision required by MLLMs. We argue that a new dataset must be purposefully designed to support three core capabilities: First, generalization, enabling models to learn shared knowledge across tasks through a unified annotation format; Second, complex scene understanding, training models to capture fine-grained object attributes and spatial relationships and to describe scenes in detailed natural language; Finally, reasoning, equipping models with high-level visual reasoning through multiturn dialogues. To this end, we present UniRS-Instruct, a high-quality, diversified, and unified multimodal instruction-following dataset for RSI understanding. UniRS-Instruct unifies diverse tasks, including image captioning, visual question answering, visual grounding, and region-level captioning, into a consistent (question and answer) format. To construct fine-grained and context-aware instruction data, we propose a hierarchical prompting strategy: at the local level, objects are identified via rotated bounding boxes to describe their fine-grained attributes and spatial relationships; at the global level, local information is integrated with the full image to generate detailed scene-level instruction descriptions through GPT-4 V. Extensive experiments on multiple remote sensing benchmarks demonstrate that MLLMs fine-tuned with UniRS-Instruct achieve superior performance in image captioning, visual question answering, and visual grounding tasks, and exhibit stronger capabilities in describing fine-grained information, uncovering implicit knowledge, and conducting complex reasoning compared with models trained on existing datasets.
author: Linrui Xu, Yuhan Wang, Ling Zhao, Wang Guo, Qiujun Li, Kewang Long, Kaiqi Zou, Wentao Yang, Dongbo Zhou

title: An Adaptive Large Neighborhood Search Driven by Reanalysis Temperature Fields for Cold-Region UAV Mission Scheduling
content: Uncrewed aerial vehicles operating in cold regions face a fundamental scheduling challenge: battery efficiency drops with ambient temperature, causing the effective range to vary dynamically over the day. Existing routing methods, however, treat range as a fixed or static parameter, producing plans that may pass nominal feasibility checks but fail under actual low-temperature execution. This article addresses the multiplatform UAV scheduling problem with time windows and payload constraints, and proposes a temperature-aware adaptive large neighborhood search (TA-ALNS) that converts the temperature-to-capacity relationship into a time-varying effective range and embeds this signal directly into the search-decision layer. Endurance is verified segment by segment at each leg’s departure time using a battery efficiency function, so that battery state participates in route feasibility evaluation rather than serving merely as a post-hoc correction. Three new operators are designed—an energy-risk guided destroy operator, a temperature-aware insertion repair operator, and a temperature-aware platform migration repair operator—that embed range margins, temperature risk, and time slack into search decisions to actively avoid high-risk legs and optimize platform assignments. On Solomon benchmark instances under real winter temperature traces, TA-ALNS achieves lower objective values in 43 out of 48 paired comparisons against the static baseline (STB), with average composite-cost improvements of 19.37% in single-platform and 10.15% in multiplatform scenarios (strongest under deep low-temperature exposure; see Section VI-G). STB solutions exhibit service-failure risks under real low-temperature execution, whereas TA-ALNS effectively circumvents high-risk long-distance legs. Ablation experiments confirm that embedding battery-aware information into search decisions, rather than using it for post-hoc evaluation only, is the key driver of performance gains, with the in-search feasibility/evaluation layer contributing most of this benefit and the temperature-aware operators a further increment. Robustness checks across two additional winter days and seven alternative battery efficiency function families indicate that the direction of the benefit is not specific to a single weather sample or a single battery model—the V-shaped model used in the headline comparison sits at the conservative end of the cross-model spectrum. We further introduce a Thompson sampling-based adaptive operator selection mechanism with principled Bayesian exploration, positioned as a run-to-run reliability enhancement: it reduces the across-run standard deviation by 46%, while remaining at least as good on the best-of-five objective used throughout the article. The method is most effective in single-platform, large-scale scenarios.
author: Jiankai Fang, Hongkun Wang, Juntao Yin, Zhihan Xu, Yan Qian, Shuo Zhang, Guangrun Hu

title: C3Former: A Spectral–Spatial Fusion Transformer for Hyperspectral Landcover Classification
content: Hyperspectral remote sensing imagery provides rich spectral–spatial information for land-cover classification, offering advantages in complex scene understanding. However, existing methods often fail to fully exploit spectral–spatial dependencies due to limited labeled samples, leading to degraded performance under low-label-ratio settings. To address this issue, a novel hyperspectral classification model, termed C3Former, is proposed to explicitly model spectral–spatial dependencies and enable multiscale feature fusion through adaptive receptive field modulation. Specifically, a dynamic hole rate grouping atrous spatial pyramid pooling module is introduced to adaptively adjust receptive fields for objects at varying scales. By leveraging deformable sampling and multirate dilated convolutions, it effectively fuses multiscale spatial contexts and enhances feature discriminability. In addition, a spectral window cross-band attention transformer module is designed to perform frequency-aware spectral decomposition and hierarchical attention modeling, capturing local spectral continuity via window-based self-attention and modeling global cross-band dependencies through a cross-band attention mechanism. Furthermore, a cross-layer convolutional-transformer encoder module is developed to reinforce spectral–spatial dependencies via cross-layer feature interaction and gated fusion. Experiments on six public datasets demonstrate that the proposed method achieves superior performance. Extensive experimental results further validate its effectiveness, robustness, and generalization under diverse conditions.
author: Chenchen Fu, Qingqing Hong, Shivakumara Palaiahnakote, Bin Li, Changwei Tan, Di Wu

title: CoastMamba: A Boundary-Enhanced Mamba Framework for Sea–Land Segmentation in Optical Remote Sensing Imagery
content: Sea–land segmentation (SLS) in optical remote sensing imagery is a fundamental task that faces significant challenges due to the complex morphology of coastlines. Shaped by diverse natural factors and anthropogenic infrastructure, coastal environments exhibit substantial spatial–temporal variability and boundary ambiguity. Existing convolutional neural networks (CNN)-based and vision Transformers-based methods often suffer from high computational costs and insufficient exploitation of frequency-domain cues, which are critical for boundary characterization. To address these issues, we propose CoastMamba, a novel SLS framework. Specifically, to mitigate background interference and structural ambiguity, a grouped coordinate Mamba (GCMamba) block is designed to generate adaptive gating masks for effective feature recalibration and selective boundary emphasis. Moreover, to handle weak contrast and blurred boundaries, a Frequency-Domain Boundary-Enhanced Module is introduced to jointly leverage spatial and frequency representations, enhancing feature discrimination. Furthermore, to preserve fine-grained local details alongside global semantics, a multilevel feature aggregation pyramid (MFAP) decoder is employed to integrate hierarchical features. Finally, to address the limitations of existing SLS datasets regarding low spatial resolution and limited scene coverage, we construct the high-resolution fine-grained Minnan Sea–Land Segmentation dataset. Extensive experiments on this dataset and public benchmarks demonstrate that CoastMamba achieves a boundary intersection over union (IoU) of 60.06%, an IoU of 96.84%, and an F1-score of 98.39%, significantly outperforming state-of-the-art methods.
author: Peng Yu, Pu Song, Xiaojing Zhong, Shengbo Chen, Wenting Wu, Guangchun Li, Weiming Xie, Hua Su

title: Leveraging Power of Deep Learning for Fast and Efficient Elite Pixel Selection in Time Series SAR Interferometry
content: This study proposes a new convolutional long short-term memory (ConvLSTM) based architecture for selection of elite pixels (i.e., less noisy) in time series interferometric synthetic aperture radar (TS-InSAR). The model utilizes the spatial and temporal relation among neighboring pixels to identify both persistent and distributed scatterers. We trained the model on ∼20 000 training images (interferograms), each of size 100 × 100 pixels, extracted from InSAR time series interferograms containing both artificial features (buildings and infrastructure), and objects of natural environment (vegetation, forests, barren or agricultural land, water bodies). Based on such categorization, we developed two models, tailormade to detect elite pixels in urban and coastal sites. Training labels were generated from elite pixel selection outputs generated from the wavelet-based InSAR (WabInSAR) software. We used four urban and seven coastal sites for training and validation, respectively, and the predicted elite pixel selection maps reveal that the proposed models efficiently learn from WabInSAR-generated labels, reaching a test accuracy of 94%. The models accurately discard pixels affected by geometric and temporal decorrelation while selecting pixels corresponding to urban objects and those with stable phase history unaffected by temporal and geometric decorrelation. The density of pixels in urban areas is comparable to and higher for coastal areas than WabInSAR outputs. With significantly reduced time computation (∼ 5 min per dataset) and improved density of elite pixels, the proposed models can efficiently process long InSAR time series stacks and generate deformation maps quickly, making the time series InSAR technique more suitable for varied (nonurban and urban) terrains and unaddressed land deformation applications.
author: Ashutosh Tiwari, Nitheshnirmal Sadhasivam, Leonard O. Ohenhen, Jonathan Lucy, Manoochehr Shirzaei

title: Machine Learning Models for Field-Scale Soil Moisture Mapping via UAS-Based GNSS-R
content: Accurate mapping of field-scale soil moisture (SM) is a critical component of precision agriculture. This study proposes a machine learning (ML)-based framework that leverages multimodal observations collected by an unmanned aircraft system (UAS) to generate high-resolution SM estimates over 210 m × 110 m (2.31 ha) corn and cotton fields at Mississippi State University’s research farm. The proposed ML approach uses in situ SM measurements acquired from SM probes as ground-truth labels. The dataset spans over three growing seasons (2021–2023) and integrates global navigation satellite system reflectometry (GNSS-R) observables, multispectral vegetation indices, light detection and ranging-derived canopy structure, and temporal features, such as day of year, to characterize dynamic soil–vegetation interactions. Three ML models, namely, random forest, extreme gradient boosting (XGBoost), and light gradient boosting machine, were evaluated under challenging cross-validation strategies to assess spatial, temporal, and cross-crop generalization. In addition, multiple feature-selection techniques were applied to identify compact and physically meaningful predictor subsets. Results show that XGBoost achieves the strongest overall performance (e.g., root-mean-squared error = 0.0324 $\text{m}^{3}\text{m}^{-3}$ under probewise validation), with realistic SM maps that align with normalized difference vegetation index and canopy height maps. A modalitywise ablation study and comparison with a classical linear regression baseline were also conducted to evaluate the contribution of individual sensing modalities and the effectiveness of nonlinear multimodal learning. A voting-based aggregation of selected features across all models and validation schemes highlights a small set of consistently informative variables related to temporal variability, UAS orientation, satellite geometry, and surface reflectivity behavior. The findings provide a detailed understanding of the opportunities and limitations of UAS-based GNSS-R SM prediction and point to promising directions for improving model generalization in future systems.
author: Md Ebtidaul Karim, Mohammad Abdus Shahid Rafi, Volkan Senyurek, Ardeshir Adeli, Huang Yanbo, John E. Ball, Ali Cafer Gurbuz

title: MST-Net: A Seabed Sediment Classification Framework Based on a Multiscale Fusion and Transformer Model Using Airborne LiDAR Bathymetry Data and WorldView-2 Images
content: Seabed sediment data can reflect the sedimentary and ecological features of a seabed and are highly important for scientific research and applications, such as marine engineering construction, ecological protection, and resource exploration. Airborne LiDAR bathymetry (ALB) systems can obtain high-precision shallow underwater full-waveform data and terrain point clouds, providing new opportunities for sediment classification. The particularity and complexity of seabed environments make it difficult for ALB data to fully reflect sediment features. Satellite remote sensing images provide multispectral information, which can be combined with ALB data to accurately classify seabed sediment. However, multisource data fusion usually causes feature redundancy, increases model computing overhead, and affects the accuracy of sediment classification. To address the above issues, a multiscale fusion and transformer neural network (MST-Net) is introduced for seabed sediment classification in shallow sea areas. First, ALB data are fused with WorldView-2 multispectral images. From the fused dataset, the terrain, waveform, and spectral features are extracted to enhance the diversity and representativeness of the input features. Second, a transformer-based self-attention module is designed to assign adaptive weights to the 25-D input features, thereby emphasizing the most informative features. Finally, a multiscale fusion module is constructed, where feature vectors extracted at different scales are upsampled using a multilayer perceptron and subsequently fused, enabling the model to effectively capture geometric structures at multiple spatial scales. The proposed MST-Net model was evaluated using fused data from the shallow coastal areas surrounding Wuzhizhou island, Hainan Province. The proposed MST-Net yielded excellent performance metrics, with an overall accuracy of 0.985, a mean intersection over union of 0.957, and a kappa coefficient of 0.934. With the precision, recall, and F1 score all exceeding 0.97, the model successfully categorized seabed sediments into coral reef, gravel, and sand. Following training, the optimal model was applied to map the sediment distribution across the shallow areas of Wuzhizhou island. The robustness and efficacy of this approach were further substantiated through rigorous comparative and ablation experiments.
author: Wenxue Xu, Yingjie Ren, Yadong Guo, Yanxiong Liu, Xue Ji, Qiuhua Tang, Jingyu Zhang, Yikai Feng

title: Cross-Level Frequency-Domain Boundary-Aware Lightweight Network for SAR Flood Detection
content: Synthetic aperture radar (SAR) has become a crucial observation tool for flood disaster monitoring due to its all-weather and all-time imaging capabilities. However, existing bitemporal SAR flood detection methods primarily rely on spatial-domain feature fusion, which often results in missed detections and false alarms when encountering irregular-boundary floods. To address this limitation, this study introduces a cross-level semantic-guided frequency boundary-aware (CSFB) module and a multiscale semantic-aware bottleneck (MSAB) module. Specifically, the CSFB module introduces deep semantic features and analyzes the frequency-domain correlation between shallow features and deep semantic features, thereby adaptively selecting frequency components from the shallow features and fusing them with the deep semantic features. Thus, this design preserves the main structure of the flood body from the shallow features, while enhancing the model’s ability to perceive flood boundary details within the high-frequency components. Furthermore, the MSAB module integrates convolutions with various dilation rates into multiscale feature fusion to establish associations between local flood details and global context information, enhancing the unified detection of both large-scale and small-scale flood regions. By integrating CSFB and MSAB modules, a novel cross-level frequency-domain boundary-aware lightweight network (CFB-Net) is proposed to enhance the perception of irregular-boundary floods. Comprehensive experiments on the S1GFloods and ETCI-2021 datasets, along with generalization evaluations on the Jubba and Weihui real-world flood events, demonstrate that CFB-Net effectively enhances the perception of irregular flood boundaries and suppresses false alarms caused by weak-scattering interference.
author: Xingye Yang, Tianyu Wei, Lyuzhou Gao, Wenchao Liu, Jue Wang, Liang Chen

title: Aerial Target Recognition Based on ISAR Images Under Incomplete Sample Conditions
content: Aerial target recognition based on inverse synthetic aperture radar imaging is a critical technology in military reconnaissance, yet it is severely challenged by the attitude sensitivity of electromagnetic scattering. Due to the noncooperative nature of targets, it is difficult to obtain a complete feature template library, which degrades recognition reliability. This article proposes a novel recognition method under incomplete sample conditions. First, a scattering center evolution model (SCEM) is developed to describe the attitude-dependent variation of dominant scattering centers in a physically constrained form. Unlike using isolated scattering centers, the SCEM couples endpoint and edge features, introducing attitude visibility and low-order evolution functions to parameterize amplitude variations. Based on sparse observations, SCEM parameters are estimated to reconstruct attitude-controllable feature templates. Furthermore, the reconstructed space is embedded into a discriminative linear subspace, where Fisher-type selection and a similarity classifier are adopted for recognition. Experiments on electromagnetic calculation and measured data confirm that the proposed method outperforms template averaging and implicit neural representation in both reconstruction similarity and recognition accuracy.
author: Hanjie Wu, Yongqiang Cheng, Rumming Zou, Runzhou Li, Kang Liu, Hongqiang Wang

title: Remote Sensing Image Destriping via Adaptive Huber-Enhanced Anisotropic TV With Statistical Feature Constraints
content: Stripe noise in remote sensing images, often caused by inconsistent sensor responses and dark current, significantly degrades image quality and complicates analysis. Existing methods are effective for regular stripe patterns, but they often rely on simplified statistical assumptions, fixed smoothness constraints, or global sparsity priors, making it difficult to simultaneously preserve structural details and characterize spatially varying stripe components in real remote sensing images. To address this, we propose a variational destriping framework integrating statistical feature constraints. A location-aware stripe variational filtering estimates statistical guidance, which is embedded into a two-dimensional variational model.An adaptive Huber-enhanced anisotropic total variation (TV) regularization suppresses staircase artifacts while preserving edges, and reweighted block sparsity captures the spatially varying sparsity of real stripe noise. The model is optimized using iterative reweighted least squares and the alternating direction method of multipliers. Experiments on simulated and real datasets demonstrate superior stripe removal and detail preservation compared to state-of-the-art approaches.
author: Zhangping Wu, Mi Wang, Ru Chen, Qianyu Wu

title: City-Scale Industrial Land Grounding and Environmental Risk Mapping With Retrieval-Augmented Vision–Language Models
content: Effective management of industrial land is essential given its substantial environmental footprint, intensive resource consumption, and implications for urban planning and public health. Accurate visual grounding of industrial parcels in remote sensing imagery provides a critical basis for assessing associated environmental risks and supporting evidence-based resource allocation. However, existing approaches often rely primarily on visual cues and remain vulnerable to domain-specific ambiguity in complex urban environments. To address these limitations, we propose retrieval-augmented geospatial vision–language grounding (RAGVLG), a model-agnostic framework that integrates structured knowledge retrieval with vision–language models (VLMs) to improve industrial land grounding in remote sensing imagery. RAGVLG retrieves domain knowledge and contextual exemplars to guide grounding decisions, enabling flexible adaptation to different VLM backbones. We construct an industrial land-grounding dataset and systematically evaluate the proposed framework, demonstrating consistent improvements over baseline VLMs across multiple backbones. We further demonstrate its utility through city-scale applications in Shenzhen and Hong Kong, where industrial land is mapped, and the spatial distribution of potential environmental risks is assessed by integrating key environmental parameters. Local indicators of spatial association are used to quantify spatial clustering of risk. The results show that high–high hotspots account for 10.62% of all grids in Shenzhen, forming a continuous coastal corridor primarily across Nanshan and Baoan Districts. Hong Kong exhibits a higher proportion of high–high clusters, at 15.31%, with more fragmented high-risk areas concentrated in Kwai Tsing and Kowloon. These findings provide quantitative and spatially explicit evidence for regional industrial planning, environmental risk management, and sustainable industrial development.
author: Yuling Wu, Xiyu Jin, Ruiqian Zhang, Qingyu Li

title: MarsMTFormer: A Unified Multitask Transformer for Martian Surface Detection and Instance Segmentation
content: Martian surface understanding plays a crucial role in planetary geoscience, supporting autonomous rover navigation and geological interpretation in deep-space exploration. However, existing deep learning methods for Martian surface analysis are typically designed for single tasks and fail to exploit shared representations across terrain detection and segmentation. Although a few multitask frameworks incorporate auxiliary geometric cues, they lack the capability for unified instance-level recognition and fail to handle the extreme scale variations and heterogeneous task imbalances inherent to Martian terrains. In this study, we propose MarsMTFormer, a unified multitask transformer framework for Martian surface object detection and instance segmentation. To address the large-scale variations and sparse contextual information in Martian terrains, we design a gated global context enhancement decoder, which introduces compact global semantic tokens and employs an adaptive gating mechanism to selectively inject scene-level context into query representations, resulting in more stable and discriminative features. Moreover, the severe long-tailed distributions of Mars data lead to heterogeneous imbalance across detection and segmentation tasks, posing significant challenges for unified multitask learning. To overcome this, we develop an adaptive multitask weighted sampling strategy that dynamically balances training by jointly modeling category frequency and task-specific performance feedback, enabling coordinated optimization across detection and segmentation tasks. Extensive experiments demonstrate that MarsMTFormer delivers competitive performance on the MarsScapes and SynMars-TW datasets.
author: Haiqiang Liu, Zhaohui Liu, Yutong Jia, Meibao Yao, Hutao Cui, Chunming Tang

title: Jointly Enhancing Representation and Supervision for Semisupervised Rotated Object Detection of Remote Sensing Images
content: Although semisupervised learning alleviates dependence on extensive labeled data, the paradigm remains suboptimal for rotated object detection due to the following limitations. First, the limited labeled data fails to provide sufficient supervision for rotated representation learning. Second, discrete pseudolabels only preserve sparse label-level supervision, discarding continuous feature-level rotation constraints. To address the problems above-mentioned, a novel semisupervised rotated object detection (SROD) model is proposed, which jointly considers dynamic feature modulation and dense feature complement to enhance rotation-sensitive representation learning and continuous rotation constraint modeling. Specifically, a feature modulation mechanism is proposed to modulate feature aggregation according to spatial rotation characteristics, thereby boosting rotation-sensitive representation learning for diverse rotated objects. Furthermore, a feature complement mechanism is proposed to introduce continuous feature-level rotation constraints, effectively complementing the discrete supervision and guiding the model to capture accurate rotation cues. Extensive experiments are conducted on the DOTA and DIOR-R datasets, and the results show that SROD improves mean average precision by 1.25 and 0.97 points, respectively, outperforming existing semisupervised rotated object detectors.
author: Lingqiang Meng, Shengkai Gao, Xin Lyu, Hongmin Gao, Zhizhong Liu, Yiwei Fang, Zhennan Xu, Xin Li

title: HARC-Net: Hierarchical Multiaxis Representation and Adaptive Residual Calibration for End-to-End SAR-to-Optical Image Translation
