content: Synthetic aperture radar (SAR) enables all-weather Earth observation; however, its inherent multiplicative speckle noise and geometry-dependent distortions pose significant challenges for SAR-to-optical image translation, often leading to structural deformation and degraded texture fidelity. To address these issues, this article presents Hierarchical MultiAxis Representation and Adaptive Residual Calibration Network (HARC-Net), an end-to-end Transformer-based regression framework that combines hierarchical multiaxis representation learning with statistics-guided skip-feature calibration to improve robustness and reconstruction quality. At the core of the proposed approach is a variable-axis sparse transformer (VASTormer) encoder, which integrates convolutional inductive bias with hierarchical multiaxis attention, including local block attention and sparse grid attention. This task-oriented encoder design enables efficient modeling of long-range dependencies while maintaining stable feature representations under speckle perturbations. To mitigate noise propagation in U-shaped architectures, we further introduce an adaptive dual attention and residual calibration (ADARC) module for skip connections. ADARC combines multistatistic spatial pooling (mean, max, min, and sum) with channelwise attention and learnable residual gating, effectively suppressing speckle-sensitive responses and improving semantic alignment between encoder and decoder features. Extensive experiments on two paired benchmarks, SEN1-2 and QXS-SAROPT, demonstrate that HARC-Net consistently achieves superior performance in both reconstruction quality and structural fidelity. The proposed method significantly reduces speckle-induced artifacts while preserving fine geometric details and linear structures. These results highlight the effectiveness of combining hierarchical local–global representation learning with statistics-guided feature calibration for robust cross-modal translation in remote sensing applications requiring geometrically consistent and noise-resilient optical reconstruction under adverse imaging conditions.
author: Yanghang Zhu, Zhijie Zhang, Mingsheng Huang, Yong Zhang

title: RDSRNet: A Recursive Decoupling Super-Resolution Network for Meteorological Remote Sensing Data
content: Deep-learning super-resolution (SR) methods can improve the spatial resolution of meteorological remote sensing data. However, existing studies have two limitations: First, meteorological remote sensing data suffer from imbalanced feature distribution: structural components (clear-sky or weak-echo regions) are spatially more extensive and continuous than detail components (strong convective regions). Under such circumstances, existing methods that directly learn the mapping from LR to HR in a unified feature space inevitably bias the optimization process toward structural components, ultimately leading to insufficient reconstruction quality of detail components; and second, most existing methods are only validated on a single type of meteorological data (e.g., radar or satellite), and their cross-data-type effectiveness remains insufficiently explored. To address these issues, this article proposes a recursive decoupling super-resolution network (RDSRNet). The recursive decoupling algorithm decomposes the original features into structural components and detail components, whose decoupling and reconstruction rely on subproblems of the same form but smaller scale. The SR result is finally obtained through the recursive reconstruction of subproblems at all levels. To better reconstruct the structural and detail components, a structural–detail feature reconstruction module is designed, which uses a dual-branch network for targeted reconstruction of the two components, alleviating the problem of poor reconstruction effect in detail regions caused by imbalanced feature distribution. Finally, the omni self-attention block is employed to complete feature fusion along both spatial and channel dimensions. In addition, a composite interaction connection is designed in the dual-branch network to amplify the differences between the two components, avoiding an average solution while ensuring the integrity of the structural component and improving the reconstruction accuracy of the detail component. Experiments on radar composite reflectivity and Himawari-9 satellite data demonstrate that RDSRNet outperforms the existing advanced methods across peak signal-to-noise ratio, structural similarity index measure, spectral angle mapper, and root-mean-square error metrics, especially achieving remarkable improvements in structural fidelity and detail clarity for convective regions. Information entropy and mean gradient magnitude are employed to analyze the two components from global and local dimensions, revealing that the detail components obtained through recursive decoupling possess richer information than the structural components; ablation studies further validate the performance contributions of our core designs.
author: Zhiren Zhou, Ziqi Zhao, Chunxu Duan, Qilin Zhang, Lin Song, Richard Mitchell

title: Transformer-Based BRDF Modeling and Normalization of MODIS Surface Reflectance Using Google Earth Engine for Agricultural Monitoring
content: The bidirectional reflectance distribution function (BRDF) describes surface reflectance anisotropy, introducing viewing-angle variability that affects time-series consistency and multisensor integration in agricultural remote sensing. Conventional BRDF correction methods rely either on semiempirical models requiring multiday compositing windows or physically based models dependent on simulated datasets, both of which involve simplifying assumptions that limit their ability to represent real surface dynamics. In contrast, this study proposes a novel data-driven, Transformer-based deep learning framework for BRDF modeling and correction that operates at the parcel level and daily temporal scale. The approach uses real Moderate Resolution Imaging Spectroradiometer (MODIS) observations from Terra (morning) and Aqua (afternoon), processed within Google Earth Engine, enabling efficient large-scale data access and same-day multiangular observations under different viewing geometries. The model takes as input Sun–sensor geometry and auxiliary surface parameters (e.g., leaf area index and soil moisture) to predict directional reflectance across spectral bands. The model was trained and evaluated on 48 344 agricultural parcels across Quebec. Predictive performance, assessed on an independent dataset of 7 084 paired observations, is highest in the near-infrared region (Band 2, R 2 = 0.758) and green band (Band 4, R 2 = 0.715), while it is moderate in the red (Band 1) and blue (Band 3) bands (R 2 ≈ 0.52), reflecting their lower dynamic range over croplands. Using the trained BRDF model, directional reflectance is normalized to a reference geometry to generate Nadir BRDF-adjusted reflectance. The effectiveness of this normalization was evaluated by comparing Terra–Aqua discrepancies before and after correction. Before normalization, Bands 2 and 4 exhibit greater divergence than Bands 1 and 3. After normalization, mean absolute differences decrease by 60%–73% across bands, and distributional overlap increases—from 0.64 to 0.89 (Band 1), 0.25 to 0.88 (Band 2), 0.63 to 0.88 (Band 3), and 0.30 to 0.81 (Band 4). The results indicate that systematic bias and viewing-angle effects are largely removed after normalization. In contrast, NDVI shows limited improvement (14%), indicating BRDF effects primarily influence absolute reflectance rather than ratio-based indices. Overall, the proposed framework improves multisensor consistency for large-scale agricultural monitoring.
author: Saeid Ojaghi, Yacine Bouroubi, Samuel Foucher, Anastase Nteziyaremye, Ariel Zannou

title: Cross-Modal Consistency-Guided Information Fusion for Hyperspectral and LiDAR Classification
content: The joint classification of hyperspectral image (HSI) and light detection and ranging (LiDAR) data plays an important role in remote sensing image interpretation and landcover mapping. However, the scarcity of labeled samples, coupled with the inherent heterogeneity of multisource data, poses significant challenges for achieving satisfactory classification performance. In this article, we propose a cross-modal consistency-guided information fusion framework that progressively exploits the inherent associations of same-class landcovers in terms of feature representation, local semantic context, and boundary structure, thereby guiding multisource information fusion for landcover classification under limited labeled samples. First, a multisource landcover feature construction scheme integrates spectral features, LiDAR-derived geometric features, and multiattribute spatial features from both modalities to establish complementary and diverse feature representations. Second, a prior-knowledge-guided pseudo-sample screening mechanism identifies high-reliability pseudo samples by evaluating joint spectral-elevation similarity within local windows centered on existing labeled samples for sample augmentation. Finally, a dual-gradient Markov random field (MRF), built upon Sobel-derived spectral and geometric gradient fields as complementary edge barriers, refines the initial classification map to enforce spatial coherence while preserving class boundaries. Experiments on three benchmark HSI–LiDAR datasets demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed framework.
author: Fanxin Kong, Jia Feng, Junping Zhang, Guangli Xu, Chao Lu, Liansuo Wei, Xinnian Guo

title: Remote Sensing Lithology Interpretation via a Response-Optimized Structure-Aware Multimodal Fusion Network
content: Lithological interpretation, a fundamental task in geological remote sensing, aims to discriminate different rock and soil types, playing a crucial role in geological mapping, resource exploration, and environmental monitoring. Although deep learning techniques have shown superior capabilities in feature extraction and generalization, their application to lithological interpretation remains challenging. These challenges primarily arise from inconsistent responses in multimodal data, which lead to redundant information that degrades model performance. In addition, conventional convolutions show limited capability in mining lithological features during multimodal fusion. To overcome these challenges, we propose a response-optimized structure-aware multimodal fusion network (ROSANet) for lithological interpretation. First, we propose a responsiveness-aware cross-modal channel substitution module to identify and replace low-response channels between modalities based on activation and normalization statistics, thereby suppressing redundant information and enhancing salient features. Second, we propose a dynamic structure-aware fusion module that fuses multimodal features through compression and reconstruction, integrating a learnable nonuniform receptive mechanism to capture lithological directional features. Furthermore, Sentinel-1 SAR data are incorporated as a complementary modality, providing scattering-based structural cues that compensate for the limitations in optical channels. Comprehensive experiments conducted on the Yingjisha dataset and the Djibouti dataset demonstrate that ROSANet achieves improvements of 2.7% in overall pixel accuracy and 4.2% in mean intersection over union compared to eight state-of-the-art models. These results verify the effectiveness and robustness of ROSANet for lithological interpretation in complex geological environments.
